# OptiSchedule — Product Roadmap

Gap analysis vs. production-ready platforms (e.g. Alteg.io).  
Goal: **bookings + reminders + payments + staff schedule + reports** for salon/service businesses.

Status: `[ ]` todo · `[~]` in progress (completed items removed from this file)

**Build policy:** Ship **product features** first → **launch & consumer app** → **lifecycle & ops** → **AI expansion** → **onboarding, pricing & Stripe plans last**. Existing AI baseline stays.

---

## ai-cmd-ext — Extend `AiCommandService` actions (plan)

**Goal:** Grow dashboard AI command coverage safely — every new product action gets a registry entry, classifier rule, handler (inline or delegated), rescue path, fixtures, and eval case — without letting `ai-command.service.ts` become an unmaintainable god-object.

**Baseline (today):**


| Metric                                          | Value                                                     | Source                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dashboard intents in registry                   | **252** (mutating subset in `DASHBOARD_MUTATING_INTENTS`) | `DASHBOARD_INTENTS` in `ai-command-registry.build.ts`                            |
| Dashboard REST ↔ AI audit                       | **~229** ops — **~58 gaps**                               | **ai-cmd-dashboard-6** (full table below **ai-cmd-provider-6**)                  |
| `executeSingleIntent` switch cases              | **~337** (multi-surface + aliases)                        | `ai-command.service.ts`                                                          |
| LEGACY_CORE intents owned by `AiCommandService` | **~51 mutate + ~19 read**                                 | `LEGACY_CORE_BINDINGS` in registry build                                         |
| `INTENT_SCHEMA` action union                    | **252** (from `DASHBOARD_INTENTS`)                        | `ai-command-intent-schema.build.ts` → `INTENT_SCHEMA` in `ai-command.service.ts` |
| Documented rules in schema appendix             | **~200+ actions**                                         | fixture constants appended to `INTENT_SCHEMA`                                    |
| Generic fallback on unknown handler             | still active                                              | `default` case → "don't know how to execute"                                     |


**Architecture policy (mandatory for every new action):**


| Layer          | Where to change                                                                              | Rule                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Registry       | `ai-command-registry.build.ts` + domain `*.util.ts` intent list                              | Add `id`, `surfaces`, `handler`, `mutating`, `sprint` **before** handler code                           |
| Classifier     | `INTENT_SCHEMA` union + `*_CLASSIFIER_RULES` in `*.fixtures.ts`                              | Extend action union; never rely on appendix-only rules                                                  |
| Dispatch       | `AiCommandService.executeSingleIntent` `switch`                                              | **One line:** `case 'x': result = await this.domain.handleX(...); break;` — no business logic inline    |
| Handler        | `Ai*Service` / `*.logic.ts` next to domain                                                   | All DB/API work lives here (match `AiCatalogService`, `AiSchedulingService`, …)                         |
| Validate       | `command-completion.validator.ts` + `ai-command-entity-params.registry.ts`                   | Required params per action                                                                              |
| Rescue         | `AiIntentRescueService` or domain `rescue*FromPrompt`                                        | Deterministic-first; regression-tested                                                                  |
| Tests          | `*.fixtures.ts` → `it.each` unit + `*.integration.spec.ts` + `eval/ai-command-eval.cases.ts` | EN/HY/RU; tag `surface: dashboard`                                                                      |
| Other surfaces | `ProviderAiCommandService`, `CustomerAiCommandService`, `PublicBookingAssistantService`      | Duplicate verbs where UI differs — **do not** route provider/customer/public through `AiCommandService` |


**Per-action definition of done** (every row in tables below):

> **Audit (2026-06):** not met globally for all **252** dashboard registry intents — see **ai-cmd-ext-gap** + REST audit **ai-cmd-dashboard-6**. Public/customer discovery (Sprints **63–65**) meets the spirit of this checklist; dashboard `ai-cmd-ext-1` param rows and `ai-cmd-ext-2` new verbs do not.

- [ ] Registry binding + access tier in `access-control.matrix.ts`
- [ ] `INTENT_SCHEMA` union entry + classifier rules wired
- [ ] `case` in `executeSingleIntent` **or** documented delegation to another surface service
- [ ] Handler + validator + entity params
- [ ] Rescue/heuristic + ≥10 NL variants in fixtures
- [ ] Eval golden cases (`npm run test:sprint14`; `test:ai-accuracy` when applicable)

## ai-cmd-customer — Public booking web + consumer mobile AI commands (plan)

**Goal:** Every customer-visible AI feature works on **both** anonymous public booking and logged-in consumer mobile, with one backend implementation per action family — no duplicate handler logic in the apps.

**Not in scope:** Dashboard admin (`AiCommandService`), provider mobile (`ProviderAiCommandService`) — tracked under **ai-cmd-ext** / **prov-exp-***.

### Architecture (one change, two surfaces)


| Surface                | User               | API entry                                 | Classifier schema                 | Handler dispatch                            |
| ---------------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| **Public booking web** | Anonymous visitor  | `POST /public/:slug/assistant`            | `buildPublicClassifierSchema()`   | `PublicBookingAssistantService.chat()`      |
| **Consumer mobile**    | Logged-in customer | Customer AI gateway (`surface: customer`) | `buildCustomerClassifierSchema()` | `CustomerAiCommandService.executeCommand()` |


**Routing rule:**


| Action family                                                                                                                                                         | Consumer mobile path                                                                                                         | Shared backend?                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Discovery & anonymous booking (`list_services`, `check_availability`, `recommend_specialists`, `book_appointment`, `list_providers`, `business_info`, `booking_help`) | `isPublicOnlyAssistantAction` → `runPublicAssistant()`                                                                       | **Yes** — wire once in `PublicBookingAssistantService`                              |
| Check-and-book compounds on mobile                                                                                                                                    | `decomposeDeterministicForSurface('customer')` → `check_providers_for_service` + `book_nearest_slot` via `AiPaymentsService` | **Shipped** — budget/rank/avail in shared compound context + `ai-payments.logic.ts` |
| Account & checkout (`book_package`, `cancel_my_booking`, `my_appointments`, gift card, promo, clinic self-service, …)                                                 | `dispatchCustomerIntent()` in `customer-ai-command.logic.ts`                                                                 | Customer-only — separate classifier rules + handlers                                |


**Definition of done (every customer feature row below):**

- [~] ≥10 NL variants per surface in fixtures; eval cases tagged `surface: public` **and** `surface: customer` (EN/HY/RU) — **partial** (**acc-2.4**)

## PostgreSQL RLS — tenant isolation (defense in depth)

**Goal:** Complement application-level `businessId` checks with Postgres row-level security so a missed filter cannot leak cross-tenant data.

Today isolation is app-layer only: `ensureMember()` + explicit `business_id` in queries. RLS adds a second enforcement boundary at the database.

- [ ] **gap-5.7** — PostgreSQL row-level security (RLS) for multi-tenant isolation
- [ ] **gap-5.7.1** — Request middleware — resolve tenant id (`businessId`) from JWT, API key, or public-booking slug; attach to request context before handlers run
- [ ] **gap-5.7.2** — Connection pool session — per request, set tenant on the DB connection (e.g. `SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id = …` via TypeORM query runner / pool hook) so all queries in that request inherit the tenant context
- [ ] **gap-5.7.3** — RLS policies on tenant-scoped tables — enable RLS + `USING (business_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true)::uuid)` on tables that carry `business_id` (bookings, customers, employees, services, schedules, gift cards, etc.); skip global tables (`users`, `businesses`)
- [ ] **gap-5.7.4** — Migration / admin bypass — dedicated DB role with `BYPASSRLS` for migrations, cron, and background jobs that legitimately operate across tenants
- [ ] **gap-5.7.5** — Tests — integration specs proving cross-tenant SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE fails at the database layer when RLS is enabled

# AI Accuracy Program — 99% accurate executions (Sprints 38–43)

**Goal:** Take AI command accuracy from the current baseline (>75% no-clarify completion) to **99% accurate executions** — meaning 99% of user prompts either execute correctly **or** ask the right clarifying question instead of doing the wrong thing.

**Core principle:** "Accurate execution" = (correct intent) × (correct parameters) × (correct execution) **OR** (honest clarify / safe refusal). A wrong action is a failure; a *good question* is a success.

### Accuracy ladder (how we climb to 99%)


| Stage            | No-clarify completion | What unlocks it                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Baseline (today) | ~75%                  | Shipped: classify + rescue + confidence routing (ai-i4), clarify (ai-d4), eval harness (gap-3.1) |
| **Stage 1**      | ~85%                  | Telemetry to *see* real failures (**acc-1**) + 10× eval set (**acc-2**)                          |
| **Stage 2**      | ~92%                  | Classification engine: few-shot + retrieval + self-verify (**acc-3**)                            |
| **Stage 3**      | ~96%                  | Smart clarification instead of wrong guesses (**acc-4**) + execution verification (**acc-5**)    |
| **Stage 4**      | **99%**               | Continuous learning loop + escalation for the last 1% (**acc-6**)                                |


**Why this order:** You cannot improve what you cannot measure. Telemetry (**acc-1**) and a large labeled eval set (**acc-2**) come first; every later sprint is measured against that eval set with a CI regression gate so accuracy never silently drops.

**Builds on existing infra (do not rebuild):** `AiGatewayService`, `classify_intent`, `AiIntentRescueService`, confidence routing (ai-i4), clarify-as-form (ai-d4), entity memory (ai-i2), conversation summaries (ai-i3), RAG (ai-i8), eval harness (gap-3.1 / ai-cmd-0.4), command outcome analytics (ai-e6), human-in-the-loop SLA (ai-e7), prompt security preflight.

## Sprint 40 — AI accuracy: classification engine

**Goal:** Make the core classify step dramatically more accurate via few-shot retrieval, self-verification, and layered fallback — measured against the **acc-2** eval set every step.

### acc-3.4 — Semantic intent matching (replace brittle regex heuristics)

**Problem:** Context/paraphrase failures — when a user phrases a request with different words that convey the same meaning (e.g. "whoever has a gap soonest" vs "first available"), the deterministic rescue layer (`ai-intent-heuristics.ts`, `ai-intent-rescue.service.ts`) misses it because every phrasing must be anticipated by a hardcoded regex. Today this is handled by literal keyword/pattern heuristics; the better approach is matching by *meaning* instead.

- [ ] **acc-3.13** — **Per-business paraphrase learning** — feed confirmed corrections and recurring phrasings into the matcher via `AiEntityMemoryService` (build on **acc-3.2**) so a business's own shorthand resolves on the first try

- [~] **acc-3.15** — **Confidence + clarify fallback** — low semantic-match confidence routes to smart clarification (**acc-4**) instead of a wrong guess; wrong-execution guardrail stays < 1% — **partial** (**pipe-1.3** confidence gate + **pipe-1.6.2** clarify path)



### pipe-1 — Confidence-gated command understanding pipeline

**Goal:** Handle semantically equivalent requests with different wording. Heuristics + primary LLM for obvious cases; low-confidence / `unknown` escalates to embedding semantic match → re-rank → rescue → self-verify → structural enrich → validate → execute. Anchors (not phrase whitelists); no entity names in bank. Dashboard first; provider / customer / public via adapters. Implements **acc-3.11**–**3.16**, **acc-3.4**, **acc-3.15**, **acc-4.7** incrementally.

**Target flow:** normalize → fast heuristics → LLM classify → confidence gate → (low: semantic + re-rank + optional narrow re-classify) → rescue → self-verify → structural enrich → validate → execute → telemetry.

**Examples:** "Book me a haircut tomorrow" (classifier 99% → skip semantic) · "My hair is getting pretty long" (unknown 20% → semantic → `create_booking`) · "I think I need a trim soon" (unknown 35% → semantic → `create_booking`).

## Sprint 41 — AI accuracy: smart clarification & disambiguation

**Goal:** When uncertain, ask the **right** question instead of guessing wrong. A perfect clarify counts as an accurate outcome.

- [ ] **acc-4** — Smart clarification & disambiguation

- [ ] **acc-4.1** — **Ask only what's missing** — drive clarify from field-level confidence (**acc-3.6**) + completion validator; never re-ask known fields; render as form (extends ai-d4)
- [ ] **acc-4.2** — **Top-2 intent disambiguation** — when two intents are close, show a 2-choice chip ("Did you mean *cancel booking* or *reschedule booking*?") instead of a generic "rephrase"
- [ ] **acc-4.3** — **Entity disambiguation** — ambiguous person/service ("book with Anna" but 2 Annas; "massage" matches 3 services) → show specific options, not free-text re-ask

- [ ] **acc-4.4** — **Answer reuse** — clarification answers persist for the session and feed entity memory (ai-i2) so the same question is never asked twice
- [ ] **acc-4.5** — **Cross-turn slot merge** — merge clarify answers into the original intent without losing earlier params (extends session merge stage)
- [ ] **acc-4.6** — **Proactive confirm on high-risk** — for bulk/destructive intents, always preview + confirm with a plain-language summary ("This cancels 12 bookings and notifies 12 customers — proceed?")

- [ ] **acc-4.7** — **"I'm not sure" over wrong action** — when confidence stays low after one clarify, return an honest "I didn't fully understand — here's what I can do" with 2–3 suggested valid commands, rather than executing a guess
- [ ] **acc-4.8** — **Clarify quality metric** — track clarify→success-on-next-turn rate (target >90%); bad clarifies (led to abandon) feed back into **acc-2** labeling

---



## Sprint 42 — AI accuracy: execution verification & rollback

**Goal:** Correct intent ≠ correct result. Verify parameter resolution and execution, and auto-rollback when the result doesn't match the request.

- [ ] **acc-5** — Execution verification & rollback

- [ ] **acc-5.1** — **Resolution accuracy guard** — verify fuzzy-resolved entities (name→employeeId, service text→serviceId, date phrase→ISO) cleared a confidence threshold; ambiguous resolution → clarify, never silently pick
- [ ] **acc-5.2** — **Plan-vs-prompt check** — before executing a workflow plan, a verification pass confirms the plan's steps actually match the user's prompt (catches "right intent, wrong scope")
- [ ] **acc-5.3** — **Preview diff for mutations** — show the calendar/catalog diff before commit on medium-risk ops (extends ai-d9 plan diff), not just high-risk

- [ ] **acc-5.4** — **Post-exec assertion** — after execution, assert the world matches intent (e.g. booking exists at requested time with requested provider); mismatch → auto-flag + offer rollback
- [ ] **acc-5.5** — **Auto-rollback on assertion failure** — reuse undo/workflow execution log (ai-d7 / gap-3.7) to revert when post-exec assertion fails; surface clear error to user
- [ ] **acc-5.6** — **Idempotency + conflict re-validation** — re-check schedule conflicts and duplicates at execute time (not just classify time); reject stale plans rather than double-book

- [ ] **acc-5.7** — **Blast-radius cap** — hard limits on a single AI command (max N bookings cancelled, max N providers, max date range); over cap → force explicit confirm or split
- [ ] **acc-5.8** — **Dry-run mode for new intents** — newly added intents ship in "propose-only" until they hit an accuracy bar on real traffic, then graduate to auto-execute (ties to ai-e5 thresholds)

---



## Sprint 43 — AI accuracy: continuous learning loop & escalation

**Goal:** Close the loop so the system keeps improving toward 99% automatically, and the last 1% escalates gracefully to a human instead of acting wrongly.

- [ ] **acc-6** — Continuous learning loop & escalation

- [ ] **acc-6.1** — **Weekly accuracy review job** — auto-compile: new failures, regressions, top confused intents, locales below target → posted to an internal review (email / dashboard)
- [ ] **acc-6.2** — **Failure → eval → fix pipeline** — every triaged failure becomes (a) a new eval case (**acc-2**) and (b) either a rescue rule (**acc-3.8**), a few-shot example (**acc-3.1**), or a prompt fix — tracked to closure
- [ ] **acc-6.3** — **Auto-alias suggestions** — recurring entity corrections become suggested aliases for admin one-click approval into entity memory (ai-i2)
- [ ] **acc-6.4** — **Accuracy ratchet** — each release raises the CI accuracy floor (**acc-2.9**) toward 99%; dashboard tracks progress on the accuracy ladder

- [ ] **acc-6.5** — **Human handoff on repeated failure** — after 2 failed clarifies on the same task, offer "Get help" → routes to staff/owner (dashboard) or support ticket (customer, reuses Zendesk gap-4.2); ties to human-in-the-loop SLA (ai-e7)
- [ ] **acc-6.6** — **Suggested-action fallback** — when classification truly fails, show the closest valid commands as one-tap chips so the user still completes the task
- [ ] **acc-6.7** — **Escalation analytics** — track escalation rate as the inverse of accuracy; target < 1% of prompts escalate; review escalations weekly for new eval cases

- [ ] **acc-6.8** — **99% gate met** — rolling 30-day: no-clarify completion ≥ 90%, (completion + good-clarify) ≥ 99%, wrong-execution rate < 1%, all three locales within 3 points of each other; documented in accuracy dashboard



### AI accuracy success metrics (Sprints 38–43)


| Metric                                                     | Baseline | Target    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------- |
| Accurate execution rate (correct exec **or** good clarify) | ~80%     | **≥ 99%** |
| No-clarify completion rate                                 | ~75%     | ≥ 90%     |
| Wrong-execution rate (undo / 👎 / corrected)               | unknown  | < 1%      |
| Clarify → success on next turn                             | ~??      | > 90%     |
| Per-locale accuracy spread (EN vs HY vs RU)                | unknown  | < 3 pts   |
| Escalation rate (human handoff)                            | n/a      | < 1%      |
| Eval set size (labeled golden cases)                       | hundreds | 2,000+    |

# Apps Adoption Program — near-99% adoption (Sprints 44–49)

**Goal:** Move the **customer (consumer app + public booking web) and mobile (consumer app + provider app)** experiences from "shipped" to "habitually used." Drive the full adoption funnel toward best-in-class, with the technically-bounded rates at **≥ 99%**: install→activation completion, push opt-in deliverability, crash-free sessions, and notification reach.

**Core principle:** Adoption = (they install) × (they activate) × (they come back) × (they invite others). Every drop-off is **measured before it is fixed**. A feature only counts as "adopted" when telemetry shows real users completing it — not when it ships.

### Adoption ladder (how we climb)


| Stage            | What it means                                                                                                              | What unlocks it                                                                 |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Baseline (today) | Apps shipped: consumer app (**gap-2.5**), provider app (Sprints 19–22), deep links, Firebase auth, provider push + offline | —                                                                               |
| **Stage 1**      | We can *see* the funnel                                                                                                    | Adoption telemetry (**adopt-1**)                                                |
| **Stage 2**      | More installs that activate                                                                                                | Acquisition + attribution (**adopt-2**) + frictionless activation (**adopt-3**) |
| **Stage 3**      | Users come back                                                                                                            | Retention, **consumer push**, lifecycle (**adopt-4**)                           |
| **Stage 4**      | Fast, reliable, trusted                                                                                                    | Performance + crash-free + ratings (**adopt-5**)                                |
| **Stage 5**      | The funnel compounds                                                                                                       | Referral + habit loops; exit gate (**adopt-6**)                                 |


**Why this order:** like the AI Accuracy Program, you cannot improve what you cannot measure. Funnel telemetry (**adopt-1**) ships first; every later sprint is scored against the same funnel so adoption never silently drops.

**Builds on existing infra (do not rebuild):** consumer `deep-link.ts` / `customer-auth.ts` / `recent-salons.ts` / `branding.ts` / `tenant-locale.ts` / `product-recommendation-analytics.ts` / `google-auth.ts`; provider `provider-native-push.util.ts` / `provider-push-deep-link.util.ts` / `provider-push-foreground.util.ts` / `offline-queue.ts` / `use-online-status.ts`; backend `analytics` module + `AiEventsService` + event-store; marketing-automation + loyalty + promo-codes modules; store listings (**gap-1.5**, **gap-2.5.10**); push & offline (**gap-2.1**, **gap-2.3**); onboarding (**gap-6.1**).

> **Note (per** `.cursor/rules/feature-ai-prompt-coverage`**):** every adoption feature that is user-visible on the customer or provider surface also needs AI command coverage (classifier rules + eval cases, EN/HY/RU). See **adopt-6.6 / adopt-6.7**.

## Sprint 44 — Apps adoption: telemetry & funnel measurement

**Goal:** Instrument both mobile apps and the public booking web so the full adoption funnel — install → first open → sign-in → first booking → repeat booking → referral — is measurable per tenant, platform, and locale. **Nothing else in this program works without this.**

Consent-gated (GDPR **compliance-1**) — no PII, businessId + anonymous deviceId only

# Near-99% Targets Program — clarify, completion, activation, push opt-in (Sprints 50–53)

**Goal:** Push four headline rates from their base-program targets to **near 99%**:


| Metric                                              | Base-program target   | This program |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------ |
| Clarify → success on next turn                      | > 90% (**acc-4**)     | **near 99%** |
| No-clarify completion rate                          | ≥ 90% (acc ladder)    | **near 99%** |
| Install → activation (signed in + 1st booking ≤ 7d) | ≥ 60% (**adopt-3**)   | **near 99%** |
| Push opt-in rate (after priming)                    | ≥ 80% (**adopt-3.5**) | **near 99%** |


**This is a stretch tier on top of the AI Accuracy (Sprints 38–43) and Apps Adoption (Sprints 44–49) programs — do those first.** The last few points are the hardest; each sprint below names the levers *and* the honest denominator that makes 99% real instead of vanity.

**Guardrail (non-negotiable):** chasing these numbers must not break correctness or trust — wrong-execution stays **< 1%** (**acc-5**) and no dark-pattern opt-ins. A metric "won" by doing the wrong thing or nagging users is a regression, not a win.

---



## Sprint 50 — Near-99%: clarify → success on next turn

**Lever thesis:** when we *do* ask, the next turn should almost always succeed — because we ask the *right* question as a *tappable* choice, carry every known param, and resolve the answer deterministically.

- [ ] **n99-1** — Clarify → success on next turn → near 99%

- [ ] **n99-1.1** — Structured clarify controls — render every clarify as the right input, not free text: date picker, provider chips, service chips, time-slot list (extend clarify-as-form `ai-command-wizard.tsx`, ai-d4); a tap resolves deterministically
- [ ] **n99-1.2** — Pre-resolved option sets — for entity ambiguity (2 Annas, 3 "massage" services) show the concrete catalog candidates, never a "type the name again" re-ask (**acc-4.3**)

- [ ] **n99-1.6** — Localized + voice/typo-tolerant answers — parse EN/HY/RU and voice-to-text answers ("tomrw", "2pm", "Աննա" all resolve); extend normalization **acc-3.7**



## Sprint 51 — Near-99%: no-clarify completion rate

**Lever thesis:** the best clarify is the one you didn't need — resolve correctly *without asking* by inferring high-confidence defaults, while **never** raising wrong-execution.

- [ ] **n99-2** — No-clarify completion → near 99%

- [ ] **n99-2.1** — High-confidence auto-fill — when a missing param is strongly inferable (last provider, "the usual" service, business default duration, current-screen context), fill it and proceed instead of clarifying; gated by field confidence (**acc-3.6**) and risk tier
- [ ] **n99-2.2** — Screen/context grounding — pass the current app context (the booking/customer/service on screen) into the command so "book this", "cancel it", "remind her" resolve without asking

---



## Sprint 52 — Near-99%: install → activation

**Lever thesis:** an install that arrived *to book a specific salon* should almost always reach a completed first booking — by restoring intent and removing every step between open and confirm.

**Reality / denominator:** 99% is meaningful on **intent-qualified installs** (deferred deep link carrying a target salon/service, **adopt-2.4**). Cold / ad / curiosity installs get a separate, lower bar — don't average them into this number.

- [ ] **n99-3** — Install → activation (intent-qualified, ≤ 7d) → near 99%

- [ ] **n99-3.1** — Deferred deep-link resume — after install, land directly on the intended salon→service→slot→**confirm** (extend `deep-link.ts` + **adopt-2.4**); no re-navigation, no re-search
- [ ] **n99-3.2** — One-tap sign-in + guest→account merge — Apple/Google one-tap (**adopt-3.1**); a guest can complete the booking and the account merges after, so sign-in is never a wall before activation
- [ ] **n99-3.3** — Pre-filled, payment-optional booking — slot pre-selected; pay-at-venue / pay-later fallback so a payment hiccup never blocks the first booking (activation ≠ payment)

- [ ] **n99-3.4** — Abandonment resume — reopen an unfinished booking exactly where it was left on next app open (**adopt-3.6**)
- [ ] **n99-3.5** — Activation concierge nudges — if not activated within 24h / 72h, a single well-timed push/email with a one-tap resume link (consumer push **adopt-4.1** + marketing-automation module)
- [ ] **n99-3.6** — Dead-end audit — instrument every step of the qualified-install funnel (**adopt-1.4**); any step with > 1% drop gets a fix ticket

### e2e-test-plan.full — Complete e2e test plan across the whole platform (planning only, not yet executed)

Per explicit user request ("plan 100% e2e cases then we will think about execution"). Inventoried the repo's actual app structure — it's larger than the "3 apps" framing used so far. Confirmed 4 top-level app codebases exist; one (`clinic-app`, package name `pollin-web`) is an **unrelated project** — not referenced in `docker-compose.yml` or `README.md`, has its own separate Cypress suite, different naming/tooling conventions — **excluded from this plan**. The other 3 are all genuinely part of this platform:

1. **`consumer-app`** (Ionic/Capacitor, native mobile) — the app tested in `consumer-app-e2e-bugs.1` and `consumer-app-api-sweep.1`.
2. **`frontend`** (Next.js, web) — bundles **three distinct surfaces in one codebase**: the staff/admin dashboard (`/(dashboard)/dashboard/*`, 23 pages), a **second, separate implementation** of the consumer booking flow (`/book/[slug]/*`, 20 pages, its own 1496-line `lib/public-api.ts` — likely to have *different* bugs than `consumer-app` despite serving the same purpose, since it's not shared code), and a web provider view (`/provider/*`, 5 pages), plus auth pages and misc marketing/embed pages.
3. **`provider-app`** (Ionic/Capacitor, native mobile) — the individual staff/provider's own app (calendar, schedule, patient chart, lab tasks), 16 pages, never tested this session.

**Planning note on methodology:** `consumer-app`'s API surface was small enough (91 calls, one file) to sweep exhaustively by endpoint before touching UI. `frontend` and `provider-app` don't centralize their API calls the same way (`frontend/src/lib/api.ts` and `provider-app/src/services/api.ts` are both thin shared axios setup, not endpoint catalogs — their calls are scattered per-page/hook), so for those two, **page/flow is the practical planning unit**; a proper endpoint inventory would be the first execution step, not something plannable up front without opening ~70 more files.

### e2e-test-plan.consumer-app-online-payment — Deep test case breakdown for online payment / Stripe checkout

Grounded in reading `consumer-checkout-return.util.ts`, `checkout-payment.util.ts`, `activation-payment.util.ts`, and the backend's `PrepaymentMode` enum. Online payment touches 4 distinct purchase kinds (single booking, multi-service, package, gift card) that each independently create a Stripe Checkout session, persist "pending checkout" state locally to survive the app losing focus while Stripe's hosted page is open, and reconcile on return. **All of this was blocked end-to-end by e2e-bug.10 (no Stripe Connect account on the original test business, `gevgas-operations-7c299253`)** — that blocker is now resolvable: a real business with Stripe Connect already linked exists in this database.

**Unblocking business found (user-confirmed): `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8` ("Pollin Clinic").** Queried directly: `settings.integrations.stripe = {connectMode: "oauth", connectCountry: "US", connectAccountId: "acct_1Tdf7aE4QO2K9D1a", connectChargeModel: "destination"}` — a real linked Connect account. Readiness for the cases below:
- 3 services, **all `prepayment_mode: "full"`** (Baby haircut $25, men's haircut $20, girl's haircut $50) — unblocks every "full prepayment" case; **no `deposit`-mode service exists on this business**, so the deposit-math cases (50%-fallback rounding, `Math.min(depositAmount, price)`) still need either a service reconfigured to `deposit` mode here, or a different business.
- `giftCards.purchaseEnabled: true` already — unblocks gift-card checkout cases directly, no settings toggle needed this time.
- 1 employee (Margarita Simonyan) with 300 `scheduling_slots` already generated — bookable immediately, no schedule-seeding required (unlike the original test business).
- 3 real customers already exist in this business, including one under the user's own email — a real, non-synthetic account to test with if preferred over a forged session.
- `settings.businessType: "other"` — despite the name, this is not a clinic-vertical business. **User confirmed: not changing it** — the M13/M14 clinic-only cases stay out of scope for this business; they'd need a genuine clinic-vertical business to unblock, not a type change on this one.
- No `multiService` settings configured — the multi-service and package checkout cases below still need that turned on for this business first, separately from the Stripe Connect unblock.

Not yet executed — recorded here per "we'll think about execution" from the prior turn. When execution starts, this is the business to point at for the online-payment section specifically.

#### Prepayment mode (`PrepaymentMode`: `none` | `full` | `deposit`) — never exercised, this business's services are all `none`

- [ ] A service with `prepaymentMode: 'full'` — confirm `prepaymentDue()` returns the full price and `showCashPaymentOption` correctly returns `false` (cash shouldn't be offered when full online prepayment is required)

Confirmed via network inspection: exactly one `gift-cards/quote` POST (no storm) and exactly one `gift-cards/checkout` POST — both single calls, no infinite loop live either. The checkout call created a real Stripe test-mode session (`cs_test_...`, `total: 50`); didn't complete the actual payment since that wasn't the point of this check, so no gift card was created (confirmed via DB — no new row).

  **Found and fixed a real, separate bug while inspecting the checkout response**: `createPublicGiftCardCheckout`'s TypeScript return type ([`public-api.ts:1064`](consumer-app/src/services/public-api.ts:1064)) was declared as `{ url, sessionId, amount, currency }`, but the backend ([`booking-payment.service.ts:562-567`](backend/src/modules/booking/booking-payment.service.ts:562)) actually returns `{ url, sessionId, draftId, total }` — confirmed against the real live response. `amount`/`currency` don't exist on the real payload; `draftId`/`total` do but were untyped. Currently harmless (grepped every call site — only `checkout.url` is ever read, in `GiftCardCheckoutPage.tsx:280`), but a latent trap: TypeScript would silently type-check code that read `checkout.amount` as a `number`, when it would actually be `undefined` at runtime. Fixed the type annotation to match the real shape. `tsc --noEmit` clean, full suite 147 files / 949 tests green (no behavior change, pure type-hygiene fix).
- [x] Subscription-plan checkout (via `createPublicBookingCheckout` with a `purchasePlanId`) — first-ever full run of this, previously blocked. **Blocker was seed data, not app code**: the seeded "Monthly Massage Plan" (`22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222`) fails `class-validator`'s `@IsUUID()` check because it's a dummy sequential string, not a real RFC4122 v1-v5 UUID (verified directly: `isUUID('22222222-...')` → `false` in both default and explicit-`'4'` mode — corrected my own initial wrong assumption that `@IsUUID()` uses a loose hex-shape regex). 4 existing `customer_subscriptions` rows reference that id as an FK, so rather than mutate it in place, inserted one new test plan with a real `uuid_generate_v4()` id on the same business/service ("QA Test Plan (real UUID)", user-approved via `AskUserQuestion`). **Confirmed live, full run**: quote resolved correctly (`servicePrice/subtotal/amountDue: 432, USD`), Stripe Checkout session created with the correct line item ("QA Test Plan (real UUID) subscription — 4 appointments over 3 months", `amount: 432, currency: USD`), completed a real test-mode payment (`4242...`), redirected back to "Booking confirmed!", and verified in the DB: 1 booking row + `customer_subscriptions` row (`status: active, appointments_remaining: 4`) with `metadata.stripePaymentIntentId`/`stripeConnectAccountId` correctly populated (from the subscription-refund work earlier this session). Deleted the test plan/subscription/booking after (no seed data left mutated).

#### Return-flow reconciliation (the most complex, least-tested part of this whole area)

- [x] **Successful payment return** for each of the 4 kinds — confirm `parseCheckoutReturnRoute` correctly recognizes both the native-app URL pattern (`/s/:slug/...`) and the web URL pattern (`/book/:slug/...`) for the same purchase kind, and that `confirmPublicBookingPayment` is called with the right `sessionId` extracted from the return URL. **Confirmed correct for all 4 kinds × both URL shapes, plus the native `optischedule://` scheme (not previously covered at all).** Web `/book/:slug/...` and consumer `/s/:slug/...` were already unit-tested for package/multi/single but not gift-card's `/s/...` form, and `optischedule://book/...` had zero test coverage anywhere in the repo for any of the 4 kinds (confirmed via grep — no spec touches `parseCheckoutReturnRoute` with an `optischedule://` URL). Ran all 8 missing combinations directly against the real function first to confirm correctness, then added them as permanent regression coverage in `consumer-checkout-return.util.spec.ts` (8 new cases: native package/multi/gift_card/single, consumer `/s/...` package/multi/gift_card, plus a `paid=1`-only edge case) — all pass. Also verified `sessionId` extraction end-to-end at each of the 4 checkout pages' `confirmPendingPayment`: `BookPage.tsx`/`PackageCheckoutPage.tsx`/`MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx` all use the same `sessionFromUrl?.trim() || pending?.sessionId` pattern before calling `confirmPublicBookingPayment(slug, sessionId)`; `GiftCardCheckoutPage.tsx` reads `params.get('session_id')` directly. All correct, no bug found.
- [x] **`session_id` query param present** vs. **`paid=1` query param present** — `isCheckoutPaymentReturnQuery` treats these as two independent signals; confirm both actually occur in practice (which does Stripe's `success_url` template use, and does the custom `optischedule://` URL scheme use the other?) and that both are handled identically downstream. **Confirmed: in practice they are never independent** — grepped every `paid: '1'`/`'paid=1'` occurrence in the backend (3 call sites: package/multi/single in `booking-payment.service.ts`, plus gift-card's literal string) and found all 4 checkout kinds' `successQuery` always concatenate `paid=1` **and** `session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}` together in one string — there is no code path that emits one without the other. `buildCheckoutReturnUrls`/`toConsumerSingleSuccessQuery` (used for both the web and native `optischedule://` surfaces, since both derive from the same `successQuery` input) preserve both signals identically — the native scheme doesn't drop `paid` or favor one over the other. So `isCheckoutPaymentReturnQuery`'s OR-check is not exercising two genuinely distinct real-world URL shapes today; it's defensive redundancy, already covered by the existing "detects payment return query signals" unit test (each signal independently sufficient) — not a bug, and left as-is since the redundancy is harmless and guards against a future URL-construction change that might drop one signal.
- [x] **Return without any query param but with pending-checkout state still in storage** — `hasPackageCheckoutPaymentReturn`/`hasMultiCheckoutPaymentReturn`/`hasSingleCheckoutPaymentReturn` all fall back to checking local pending-checkout storage even with no URL signal at all; confirm this correctly resumes an abandoned-then-reopened checkout, and does NOT falsely trigger for a genuinely fresh, unrelated visit to the same checkout page. **Found and fixed a real, severe bug — see e2e-bug.182b below.** Confirmed live: it DOES falsely trigger. Seeded a stale (10-day-old) `consumer_pending_package_checkout_payment` localStorage entry for a real package, then navigated fresh to that same package's `/checkout` URL with zero query params (simulating a bookmark/history/relaunch visit, not a Stripe redirect). Instead of the normal checkout flow, the page silently substituted the stale, **past-dated** schedule from storage (01/06/2026, before "today" 21/07/2026) with no banner or explanation, fired 3 concurrent `confirm-payment` POSTs against the long-dead session id (all correctly `400`'d server-side, so no data-integrity issue), and then got permanently stuck showing an "I completed payment" retry button with no visible error and no way back to a normal checkout — every subsequent visit to that same package would repeat this loop forever. Root cause: `loadPendingPackageCheckoutByPackage`/`loadPendingMultiCheckoutBySlug`/`loadPendingCheckoutPayment` had no TTL at all (confirmed via grep — `updatedAt` was written on save but never read back anywhere), and `PackageCheckoutPage.tsx`'s/`MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx`'s confirm-failure catch blocks were fully silent (`catch { return false; }`, unlike `BookPage.tsx`'s already-fixed e2e-bug.181).
- [x] **Stale/expired pending-checkout state** — what happens if a customer starts checkout, does nothing for days, then reopens the app to the same page? Is there any TTL/expiry on the pending-checkout storage, or does it persist and reconcile indefinitely? **Confirmed: no TTL existed at all — persisted and got treated as "returning from Stripe" indefinitely.** Fixed as part of e2e-bug.182b (below): added a 24h max-age check (matching Stripe Checkout Sessions' own default lifetime — anything older could never legitimately confirm anyway) to all 3 pending-checkout readers, and surfaced the existing `checkoutPaymentPendingRetryMessage` copy on a failed confirm in the package/multi checkout pages instead of failing silently. Re-tested live with the identical 10-day-old stale entry after the fix: the same fresh, no-query-param visit now correctly redirects to a normal, current "Schedule package" flow (today's date, no stale data, zero confirm-payment calls) instead of hijacking into the stuck retry loop. Added regression coverage (TTL fresh-vs-stale cases) to all 3 storage-util spec files.
- [x] **Query-param merge on return** (`mergePackageCheckoutReturnQuery`/`mergeMultiCheckoutReturnQuery`) — reconstructing `lines`/`services` from pending-checkout storage when the return URL itself doesn't carry them; confirm this correctly restores the exact original selection (services, employee, times) rather than a stale or empty cart. **Confirmed correct, via a real end-to-end multi-service Stripe payment** (temporarily reactivated the dormant `prepaymentMode: 'full'` "QA Concurrency Test" service, same one used earlier this session): booked "Neck Massage" + "QA Concurrency Test" together at a distinctive 13:00 slot with a specific specialist, paid via real Stripe test-mode checkout, and verified the DB afterward — both bookings landed at the exact selected times (17:00–17:50 / 17:55–18:25 UTC, i.e. 13:00–14:25 local, back-to-back as scheduled) with the exact correct specialist, `multi_service_group_id` correctly linking them, `paymentStatus: paid`. **Key finding: the backend's own multi-service `success_url` never carries schedule details at all** — confirmed via source (`booking-payment.service.ts` builds `successQuery` as only `paid=1&services=<ids>&session_id=...`, no `startTime`/`employeeId`/`lines`) and via the live Stripe page's own "Back to..." cancel link (`canceled=1&services=<ids>`, same omission). So `mergePackageCheckoutReturnQuery`/`mergeMultiCheckoutReturnQuery`'s job is cosmetic/display-only (restoring enough state so the checkout page can render "your booking: X, Y at Z" while waiting) — the actual booking correctness on return doesn't depend on the frontend reconstructing the schedule at all. `confirmPendingPayment` only needs `session_id`; the real services/times/employee are fulfilled from the **backend's stored checkout draft** (captured once at initial checkout-session creation, before ever redirecting to Stripe), so even if the merge produces a temporarily incomplete local render, the actual booking that gets created is always exactly right. For packages specifically, `mergePackageCheckoutReturnQuery` additionally has the *full* `lines` (serviceId+employeeId+startTime) in local storage as a straight JSON round-trip, so its local restore is exact too, not just cosmetically close. Cleaned up the test booking pair and re-deactivated "QA Concurrency Test" after.
- [x] **Native custom URL scheme** (`optischedule://book/:slug/packages/:packageId/checkout`, `.../multi/checkout`, `.../gift-cards/checkout`) — these are 3 of the 4 kinds; notably **no native-scheme pattern exists for single-service checkout** in `readCheckoutReturnFromUrl` (only `webSingle` — the `/book/:slug/checkout` **web** pattern requiring a `serviceId` query param — is handled; there's no `optischedule://` branch for single-service at all). Worth confirming whether single-service Stripe returns are actually handled via a different mechanism on native, or whether this is a genuine gap where a native single-service payment return could fail to route back into the app correctly. **Checklist's premise is outdated — the native single-service branch already exists and works.** `readCheckoutReturnFromUrl` has a dedicated `optischedule://book/{slug}/{serviceId}?…` branch explicitly labeled `// e2e-bug.18 — native single-service return`, confirmed present in source and confirmed working via a direct probe (`optischedule://book/salon/svc-1?paid=1&startTime=...&session_id=cs_single_native` → correctly resolves `{kind: 'single', serviceId: 'svc-1', ...}` with `session_id` extracted). This test gap (zero prior spec coverage of the native scheme for any of the 4 kinds) was already closed 2 items ago in this same pass — added as permanent regression tests in `consumer-checkout-return.util.spec.ts` (native package/multi/gift_card/single, all passing). No gap exists; the checklist item likely predates e2e-bug.18's fix landing.
- [x] **Cancelled/abandoned checkout** (user closes Stripe's hosted page without paying) — confirm the app correctly detects "no payment happened" rather than assuming success, and that the pending-checkout state either clears or remains resumable as appropriate. **Confirmed correct, live, via a real Stripe test-mode checkout abandoned mid-flow**: started a real single-service checkout (QA Concurrency Test, $40), then clicked Stripe's own "Back to..." link *without* paying (`cancel_url`, confirmed to carry only `canceled=1&employeeId=...&slot=...&date=...` — no `session_id`/`paid=1`). The app correctly did **not** assume success: it still auto-attempted `confirm-payment` (via the pending-storage fallback, since the storage entry is fresh, not stale), got a correct `400` from the backend (payment not complete), and showed the real "We couldn't confirm your payment yet..." retry message + "Waiting for payment" banner (the e2e-bug.181 fix) — no false "Booking confirmed!" anywhere. Pending state correctly remained resumable: clicking the primary CTA again created a genuine **new** Stripe checkout session (verified via network log — a fresh, different `session_id`), so the customer isn't stuck. **Minor, non-blocking observation, not fixed**: the primary CTA's label logic (`confirmButtonLabel` in `BookPage.tsx`) checks `if (awaitingPaymentReturn) return 'Complete payment…'` before checking anything else, and `awaitingPaymentReturn` only resets on a *successful* confirm — so after a cancelled/failed attempt the button stays mislabeled "Complete payment…" (implying "resume what you started") even though clicking it actually starts an entirely fresh checkout session, not resuming the old one. Functionally harmless (verified the click does the right thing), just a confusing label — flagged for a future polish pass, not fixed here (out of scope for a "does it work correctly" pass, matching this session's established practice of noting-but-not-fixing pure cosmetic CTA-label mismatches, e.g. the earlier `MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx` CTA-label note in this same section).
- [x] **Double-confirmation** — call `confirmPublicBookingPayment` twice with the same `sessionId` (e.g., user double-taps back into the app, or a retry fires) — confirm idempotent handling, not a duplicate booking or duplicate charge. **Confirmed idempotent, live**: completed a real single-service Stripe payment (QA Concurrency Test, $40, real test-mode card), then directly replayed the exact same `confirm-payment` call a second time (sequentially, well after the first had already succeeded) with the identical `sessionId`. The second call correctly returned `{"alreadyCompleted": true}` (still `201`, not an error) and a DB check confirmed **exactly one** booking row for that session — no duplicate booking, no duplicate charge (Stripe itself was only asked to create one PaymentIntent in the first place; re-confirming the same session never asks Stripe to charge again). This is the same `fulfillDraft` code path hardened by e2e-bug.182 earlier in this pass (the atomic `draftRepo.update` claim) — that fix targeted the *concurrent*-request race specifically, but the simpler *sequential* double-confirm case (this checklist item's literal scenario) was already safe beforehand too, via the pre-existing `if (draft.status === 'completed') return { alreadyCompleted: true }` check, and remains safe now. No bug found.

#### Payment failure / edge cases (Stripe test-mode card numbers make these directly testable once Connect exists)

- [x] Card decline (Stripe's `4000000000000002` test card) — confirm the failure surfaces a sane message, not a raw error (cross-check against the e2e-bug.3 pattern — this is a very plausible 7th instance). **Not a 7th instance — the e2e-bug.3 pattern structurally cannot occur here.** Tested live with the real decline card on a real Stripe Checkout session: Stripe's own hosted page shows a clean, native message — "Your credit card was declined. Try paying with a debit card instead." — entirely within Stripe's UI. Our app is never even involved: a card decline is handled client-side by Stripe's own hosted checkout page with **zero network round-trip back to our backend**, so there is no code path in the consumer-app where a raw axios/HTTP error string could leak through for a decline specifically (unlike e2e-bug.3's other 6 instances, which all involve a real request to *our* backend whose error response then gets mishandled). The customer stays on Stripe's page and can immediately retry with a different card in the same session (confirmed — see next item, retried on the identical session). The only way this scenario touches our app at all is if the customer subsequently abandons/returns without fixing the card, which is exactly the already-tested "cancelled/abandoned checkout" path (2 items up) — already confirmed to show a sane retry message, not a raw error.
- [x] 3D Secure / SCA challenge (Stripe's `4000002500003155` test card) — confirm the challenge flow completes and returns correctly. **Confirmed correct, live, end-to-end.** On the same Stripe session as the decline-card test above, retried with the 3DS test card — Stripe correctly presented its test 3D Secure 2 authentication modal ("This is a test 3D Secure 2 authentication for a transaction with INSTAGRAM.COM/HILLS_SP", Complete/Fail buttons). Clicked "Complete", and the flow finished exactly like a normal payment: redirected back to the app, showed "Booking confirmed!", and the DB confirmed a normal `status: confirmed, paymentStatus: paid` row with a real `stripePaymentIntentId` — structurally identical to a non-3DS payment, no special-casing needed or missing on our side. No bug found.
- [x] Insufficient funds / other specific decline codes — confirm distinct, sane messaging per code where Stripe provides one. **Confirmed distinct and sane across 4 codes, live, on the same real Stripe Checkout session used for the generic-decline test above.** `4000000000009995` (insufficient_funds) → "Your credit card was declined because of insufficient funds. Try paying with a debit card instead." (a genuinely more specific variant of the generic decline text, not a copy-paste duplicate). `4000000000000069` (expired_card) → "Your card is expired. Try a different card." — caught entirely client-side (Stripe's own card-element validation flags the expiry field red before any submission network call is even made). `4000000000000127` (incorrect_cvc) → "Your card's CVC is incorrect." — round-trips to Stripe's network for the check (CVC can't be validated client-side) but still surfaces a specific, correct message. All 4 messages (this trio plus the earlier generic-decline one) are distinct from each other, correctly worded per failure reason, and — same structural point as the generic-decline item above — entirely rendered by Stripe's own hosted Checkout page with zero round-trip to our backend, so there is no code path in our app that could mangle or genericize any of them. No bug found.
- [x] Network interruption mid-redirect-to-Stripe or mid-return-from-Stripe — does the app recover, or does it leave the customer in a stuck/ambiguous state about whether they were charged? **Confirmed recovers correctly for the reproducible case; one real but narrow, largely dev-environment-specific gap found and documented (not fixed — see reasoning below).**

  **Mid-redirect-to-Stripe, live-reproduced**: started a real checkout (QA Concurrency Test, $40), clicked "Pay & confirm booking" on Stripe's hosted page with a valid card, then immediately force-navigated the tab away to `example.com` before Stripe's own redirect back to our app could occur (simulating a connection drop right as the customer submits payment). Checked the backend directly afterward: the `booking_checkout_drafts` row for that session (`abbfaafe-d9af-4a9b-bc60-221720feaf5c`) was still `status: pending` — Stripe itself never completed the charge (confirmed via the backend's own subsequent check: `"Payment is not complete yet"`), so no money moved and no booking was silently created (verified — no new row in `bookings`). Revisiting the exact same book page afterward correctly self-healed: the existing pending-checkout-storage fallback (the same mechanism validated earlier this session for the "cancelled/abandoned checkout" case) auto-retried `confirm-payment`, got the same accurate `400`, and displayed the already-existing sane retry copy ("We couldn't confirm your payment yet. If you completed checkout, please wait a moment and try again.") — not a raw error, not a false "Booking confirmed!". The customer is left in a **clear**, not ambiguous, state: nothing was charged, and the same "Pay & confirm booking" button remains available to retry.

  **Mid-return-from-Stripe (charge succeeds, but the return trip itself is interrupted before the app confirms)** — this specific sub-case could not be forced with millisecond precision through browser automation (Stripe's post-payment redirect and our app's confirm call both fire client-side within the same page load, too fast to reliably race), so this was verified by mechanism instead of by a live race: 
  - The recovery code path is identical regardless of *why* the customer didn't see a confirmation — `hasSingleCheckoutPaymentReturn`'s pending-storage fallback re-calls `confirm-payment` with the stored `sessionId` on any revisit to the same page, and that endpoint is already proven idempotent and safe (this session's e2e-bug.182 atomic-claim fix, plus the double-confirmation idempotency check above). So as long as the customer revisits the same device/browser, a successful-but-unconfirmed charge resolves cleanly and automatically — already effectively covered by the "cancelled/abandoned checkout" and "double-confirmation" items above, which exercise the same fallback machinery.
  - **The one real gap**: if the customer does *not* revisit the same page (different device, storage cleared, or they simply check "My Bookings" instead), there is no proactive signal at all. Confirmed via code: `AccountPage.tsx` (grepped for `loadPendingCheckoutPayment`/`hasSingleCheckoutPaymentReturn`/`confirmPublicBookingPayment` — zero matches) never checks pending-checkout state in the background, so a successful-but-unconfirmed payment simply doesn't appear anywhere the customer would look. The only proactive-feeling recovery is the existing (already-built, not new) AI-assistant intent `resume_pending_payment` (`ai-resume-pending-payment.logic.ts`) — but it's opt-in, triggered only if the customer explicitly asks something like "I closed the app mid-checkout," not surfaced automatically.
  - **Why this is narrower in practice than it sounds, and why not fixed here**: in this specific local dev environment, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (`backend/.env`), and `billing.service.ts` explicitly throws `BadRequestException('STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured')` before ever processing a `checkout.session.completed` event — confirmed this is a safe, deliberate no-op (not an insecurely-bypassed check), meaning the webhook safety net that a **production** deployment would have (reconciling a paid-but-unconfirmed session independently of the client, typically within seconds) simply cannot be exercised or demonstrated locally. So the worst-case customer impact of this gap is environment-dependent: in production, the booking would very likely still show up in "My Bookings" shortly on its own via the webhook even if the client-side confirm never fires; only the *proactive notification* piece (telling the customer sooner, without them needing to refresh/reopen "My Bookings" or think to ask the AI assistant) is actually missing everywhere, dev and prod alike. Building a proactive "you have a payment awaiting confirmation" banner on `AccountPage.tsx` is a real, reasonable polish item, but it's a UI feature addition rather than a correctness bug — flagged here for a future pass rather than built in this one, consistent with this session's established practice of noting-but-not-fixing scope-expanding UX nicities (e.g. the CTA-label observations earlier in this section) when the underlying data/money handling itself is already safe.

#### Refunds (cross-reference: this session's earlier work already built refund logic for bookings/subscriptions/packages/gift cards, all sharing the `'refunded' | 'already_refunded' | 'skipped' | 'failed' | 'ineligible'` status shape)

- [x] Cancel a paid-online booking within the allowed window — confirm the refund actually fires (Stripe test mode shows the refund on the payment intent) and the UI communicates the right one of the 5 refund-status outcomes to the customer. **Found and fixed two real, severe bugs — see e2e-bug.184 and e2e-bug.185 below.** First live attempt (a real paid booking, 6 days out — well within the cancellable window) hit a **500 crash** on the very first try, not a refund at all: `"FOR UPDATE cannot be applied to the nullable side of an outer join"` — a raw Postgres error leaking straight through the API, meaning booking cancellation was **completely broken** for any booking whose cancel reached the actual lock/refund code path (e2e-bug.184, fixed). After fixing that, re-ran the exact same cancel and it succeeded correctly: `refundStatus: "refunded"`, and — going one step further than just trusting the app's own response — queried **Stripe's API directly** or the refund id returned (`re_3TvZBV81m04mcCIP1HZqPfaN`) and confirmed independently: `status: "succeeded"`, `amount: 4000` ($40.00), correctly tied to the original `payment_intent`. Then found the second bug while checking whether the UI actually shows this: it doesn't — `ConsumerBookingActions.tsx`'s cancel handler discarded the entire API response (typed as `unknown`) and never read `refundStatus` at all, so a customer whose refund had genuinely **failed** (Stripe error, expired card, etc.) would see the exact same silent "cancelled" outcome as one whose refund succeeded, with zero indication their money hadn't come back (e2e-bug.185, fixed).
- [x] Cancel a paid-online booking where the service has already been used/partially delivered — confirm `ineligible` status surfaces with a clear explanation, not a generic failure. **Plain bookings don't use the `ineligible` refund-status shape at all** (confirmed via source: `BookingRefundStatus` only has `'refunded' | 'already_refunded' | 'skipped' | 'failed'`, no `ineligible` — that value is specific to the usage-gated subscription/package refund logic built earlier this session). For a single-visit booking, "already used" is instead handled one level up: `evaluateCustomerBookingPolicy` blocks **cancellation itself** once `status === 'completed'`, so refund logic is never even reached. Confirmed this is correct and clear both in the UI (completed bookings in the account page show no cancel button at all — just inline text "Completed appointments cannot be changed") and at the raw API level (direct call to `me/bookings/:id/cancel` on a real completed, paid booking → clean `403 {"message": "Completed appointments cannot be changed"}`, not a generic error). **Found and fixed a related, smaller bug while testing the adjacent `in_progress` case** ("partially delivered," i.e. the visit is currently happening): the policy function had no explicit check for `in_progress`, so it fell through to the notice-window check, which reads the (already-past) `startTime` and correctly blocks the cancel — but with the misleading reason `"Changes must be made at least 24 hours before your appointment"`, implying a timing/notice problem rather than "this appointment is happening right now." Live-reproduced (temporarily set a real paid booking to `in_progress` with a startTime 10 minutes in the past), fixed by adding an explicit `in_progress` branch with an accurate reason, and re-verified the corrected message live (e2e-bug.183).
- [x] Double-cancel (already-refunded booking) — confirm `already_refunded` is idempotent and doesn't attempt a second Stripe refund call. **Confirmed idempotent at every layer, live, on the already-cancelled/refunded test booking from the item above.** Called `me/bookings/:id/cancel` twice more on a booking already `status: cancelled, paymentStatus: refunded`. Both calls returned a clean `200` with the same, unchanged `stripeRefundId` — cross-checked directly against Stripe's own refunds list for that payment intent (`GET /v1/refunds?payment_intent=...`), which shows exactly **one** `succeeded` refund, not two. Traced why: `cancelBookingInternal` (`public-customer-booking.service.ts:480`) short-circuits on `booking.status === CANCELLED` and returns immediately, before ever calling `bookingService.cancel()` or any refund code — so the customer-facing surface can't even reach Stripe on a repeat call. The staff/dashboard surface (`BookingService.cancel()`) has a second, independent guard: it detects `locked.status === CANCELLED` under the row lock and returns `didCancel: false`, then unconditionally calls `attemptCancelRefund()`, which itself no-ops via `bookingNeedsOnlineRefund()` returning `false` once `metadata.stripeRefundId` is set — confirmed by the existing "does not overwrite an already-cancelled row under the lock" unit test (`booking.service.cancel.spec.ts`), which already asserts `refundBookingPayment` is never called in this case. **One real but minor gap noted, not fixed**: the customer-facing double-cancel response is a bare `{ booking }` with no `refundStatus` key at all (not even the literal `'already_refunded'`) — so a repeat cancel call is money-safe but silently uninformative rather than explicitly confirming "already refunded." In practice this is very hard to trigger through the normal UI (the cancel button disappears once a booking is cancelled — `booking.canCancel` becomes false), so it would only surface via a stale page, two open tabs, or a replayed request. Left as a documented observation rather than fixed, matching this session's established bar for narrow, low-severity, hard-to-naturally-trigger gaps once the underlying money handling is already provably safe.
- [x] Package visit refund — same 5-outcome check, specifically for the "any line already completed" ineligibility rule already implemented in a prior session. **Found and fixed a real, direct sibling of e2e-bug.185 — see e2e-bug.186 below.** Read `cancelPackageVisitInternal` (`public-customer-booking.service.ts:598`): it computes `wasUsed` from the pre-cancel snapshot (any line `COMPLETED`/`IN_PROGRESS`/`NO_SHOW`) and only attempts `packageRefundService.refundPackagePayment(...)` when `!wasUsed` — correctly gating the refund on usage exactly as designed. But like plain bookings, `PackageRefundStatus` has no `'ineligible'` literal (only `'refunded' | 'already_refunded' | 'skipped' | 'failed'`) — an ineligible-due-to-usage cancel simply leaves `refundStatus` as `undefined`, identical to a plain cash package with nothing to refund. **e2e-bug.186**: `ConsumerPackageVisitActions.tsx`'s `handleCancel()` called `cancelCustomerPackageVisit`/`cancelPackageVisitWithToken` and discarded the entire response (`await cancelCustomerPackageVisit(...)` with no captured variable) — so a package visit cancel whose refund had genuinely **failed** looked identical to one that succeeded or one that was never eligible, with zero indication to the customer either way. The `public-api.ts` client function's TypeScript return type didn't even declare `refundStatus`, despite the backend already returning it (same class of type/backend mismatch as the gift-card checkout bug found earlier this session). Fixed by adding `refundStatus` to both client function return types (`public-api.ts`), capturing the result in `handleCancel()`, and rendering the same `cancelBookingRefunded`/`cancelBookingRefundFailed` copy already used by the plain-booking component (`ConsumerBookingActions.tsx`) on `'refunded'`/`'failed'` respectively — reusing existing, already-translated copy rather than adding new strings. Verified with 3 new unit tests (`ConsumerPackageVisitActions.spec.tsx`): shows the refunded notice, shows the refund-failed notice, and shows no notice when `refundStatus` is absent (covering both the ineligible-due-to-usage case and the plain-cash/no-refund-owed case, which are indistinguishable at this layer — matching the identical, already-accepted design for plain bookings). Not live-Stripe-reproduced end-to-end (this test business's packages are all `prepaymentMode: 'none'`, so no package purchase here has ever gone through Stripe — would require provisioning a new online-payment package purchase from scratch); verified instead via full type-checking (`tsc --noEmit`, zero new errors) and the full consumer-app suite (147 files / 966 tests, all green).

**e2e-bug.186 re-verification (2026-07-29), guru manual QA pass — confirmed still fixed, plus expanded coverage.** This entry only ever had this inline writeup, no separately-indexed closure record, so re-verified from scratch. Read the current `ConsumerPackageVisitActions.tsx` and `public-api.ts` — the fix described above is genuinely still in place: `handleCancel()` captures `result` and branches on `result.refundStatus === 'refunded' | 'failed'`; both `cancelCustomerPackageVisit` and `cancelPackageVisitWithToken` in `public-api.ts` correctly declare `refundStatus` in their return types.
