- [x] Screen reader (VoiceOver/TalkBack) full read-through of at least the booking flow and account page — announced order, redundant/missing labels beyond the specific role gaps already found. **No real device/VoiceOver session available, so I approximated via the accessibility tree and raw DOM ARIA attributes (same method as this session's other a11y checks) — found a new, concrete, confirmed defect beyond the already-known role gaps.** On the single-service checkout page (`/book/{serviceId}`, guest step), the 3 core contact fields — "Your name", "Email", "Phone" — are each built as a separate `<ion-label position="stacked">` sibling next to an `<ion-input>` inside an `<ion-item>` (the older Ionic pattern, not the newer `label`/`labelPlacement` prop API). Verified directly in the DOM (not just the simplified accessibility-tree view, to rule out an abstraction artifact): each `ion-label`'s `id` is an **empty string**, and the corresponding `ion-input` has no `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` of its own either — so there is no programmatic association between the visible label text and its input at all. A screen reader would very likely announce these as unlabeled edit fields (or fall back to a generic "text field" with no name), even though the labels are clearly visible on screen. **Also confirmed**: the 5 time-slot buttons on the same page (`14:00`, `14:30`, etc.) have no `aria-pressed` (or any other selected-state attribute) on the raw `<button>` elements — a screen reader has no way to announce which slot (if any) is currently selected as the user tabs through them, purely visual state. Not fixed here (three-field label-association fix plus a slot-button `aria-pressed` wiring, both small and localized, but out of scope for a pure test-and-report pass) — flagged as concrete, verified defects rather than a speculative "should probably check this."
- [x] Dynamic type / OS font-scaling — set the device font size to its largest setting and check for text truncation/overlap across the app's mostly-inline-styled components (this codebase uses a LOT of hardcoded `fontSize` pixel values in inline styles, e.g. throughout `ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx` — worth checking whether any of it respects OS text-scaling at all, or whether it's all fixed-size and therefore inherently non-scaling). **Found a real, two-layered, fully-confirmed bug — a genuine dynamic-type feature was built and then left non-functional, on top of not covering most of the app's text anyway.** First layer: there IS a purpose-built font-scaling system already in the codebase (`lib/mobile-a11y.util.ts` + `theme/adoption-a11y.css`, tagged `adopt-5.6`) — a `--adoption-font-scale` CSS custom property drives `--adoption-body-font-size`/`--adoption-caption-font-size` (`calc(1rem * var(--adoption-font-scale))`), applied via an `adoption-a11y-root` class on `<body>`. But `resolveMobileFontScale()` (the function meant to compute the real value from the device's actual text-size setting) is hardcoded: `return MOBILE_A11Y_FONT_SCALE_DEFAULT` (`= 1`) — it never reads any real OS/Capacitor accessibility setting at all, so in production this always applies a scale of exactly 1.0 (no scaling), regardless of what the customer's actual device font size is set to. Second layer, confirmed live even assuming the first were fixed: manually set `--adoption-font-scale: 3` directly (simulating what a working "largest OS text size" would look like) and screenshotted the home page — ambient, unstyled text (headings, paragraphs that don't set their own `fontSize`) *did* balloon to ~3x size via ordinary CSS inheritance from body. But then opened the AI assistant widget on the *same* page at the *same* scale and screenshotted it too: every piece of its text ("Booking assistant", the suggestion chips, "Ask anything…", etc.) rendered at completely normal, untouched size — because `ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx` (and ~130 other `fontSize: <number>` inline-style call sites across the consumer-app, confirmed via grep — vs. 122 legitimate `rem`/`em` usages elsewhere that *would* respond if the scale itself worked) hardcodes pixel values that unconditionally override any inherited font-size, CSS variable or not. So even a fully-fixed `resolveMobileFontScale()` would only visibly affect a narrow slice of the app (bare/unstyled text, plus the couple of generic selectors — `.salon-card`, `[role='dialog'/'status'/'alert']` — that `adoption-a11y.css` explicitly wires to the scale vars); the rest, including the entire assistant widget, would remain fixed-size on the largest possible device text setting. Not fixed here (this spans a stubbed core function plus ~130 individual inline-style call sites) — flagged with both the missing input (`resolveMobileFontScale`) and the narrow-scope consumption (`adoption-a11y.css`'s short selector list) as the two concrete things to address.
- [x] Reduced-motion OS setting — any animated transitions (panel open/close, spinners) that should respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. **Mixed result: page-level custom CSS correctly respects it; every `IonSpinner` in the app does not, and can't via this mechanism.** `theme/adoption-a11y.css` has a real, broad `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .adoption-a11y-root *, ...*::before, ...*::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; ... } }` rule — a universal descendant selector, not a narrow allowlist, so this correctly reaches any plain page-level CSS animation/transition (confirmed one real example: `.consumer-ai-fab`'s hover `transition: background-color 120ms ease` in `variables.css` is plain top-level CSS the rule would catch). The "panel open/close" half of this item turned out to be moot — grepped `ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx` and the theme files for any transition/animation tied to the assistant panel opening/closing and found none; it appears to mount/unmount instantly with no motion to begin with, so there's nothing to reduce there. **The real, confirmed gap is spinners.** `IonSpinner` (used extensively for loading states throughout the app — checkout pages, login, gift-card checkout, etc.) is an Ionic web component whose animations (`spinner-rotate`, `spinner-fade-out`, `spinner-circular`, etc.) are defined entirely inside its own Shadow DOM, injected via a JS template string in `node_modules/@ionic/core/dist/esm/ion-spinner.entry.js` — confirmed via direct read of that bundled CSS that it contains **zero** `prefers-reduced-motion` handling of its own. Because these animations live inside the component's shadow root, the app's own page-level `.adoption-a11y-root *` selector **cannot reach them at all** — CSS from the outer document doesn't pierce shadow DOM boundaries. Net effect: every spinner in this app will keep animating at full speed regardless of the customer's OS-level reduced-motion preference, with no code path anywhere that could catch it short of Ionic fixing this upstream or the app switching away from `IonSpinner`/wrapping it with a `::part()`-based override (Ionic's spinner doesn't expose a `part` for its animation, confirmed in the same file, so even that workaround isn't available today without an Ionic version bump). Not fixed here — this is an upstream Ionic limitation as much as an app-level one.
- [x] Color contrast — spot-check the many inline hex colors (`#6b7280`, `#9ca3af`, etc. seen throughout) against WCAG AA on both light backgrounds and the primary-color-tinted bubble backgrounds. **Computed exact WCAG contrast ratios (standard relative-luminance formula) for the most common hardcoded text colors against both plain backgrounds and the real, exact alpha-blended assistant-bubble tint for this test business — not an approximation.** Fetched this business's actual `primaryColor` (`#ff00dd`, a bright magenta — confirmed via the public profile API) and computed the exact result of the assistant's own `${primary}14`/`${primary}33` alpha-blend-over-white bubble backgrounds (`#ffebfc` and `#ffccf8` respectively) rather than guessing. Results for the most-used grays (frequency via grep across the whole consumer-app): **`#6b7280` (143 occurrences — the single most common text color in the entire app)**: 4.83:1 against pure white (passes AA normal-text's 4.5:1 minimum, but only barely), degrading to 4.27:1 against the lighter assistant-bubble tint and 3.51:1 against the stronger tint — both **fail AA for normal-size text** (would need to be large/bold text, ≥18px/24px-equivalent, to only need the 3:1 threshold both still clear). **`#9ca3af` (12+ occurrences, confirmed via source read to be used for real informational body text — "no slots available", "no reviews yet", package strikethrough prices, section labels in `ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx`, `ProviderProfilePage.tsx`, `SalonProfilePage.tsx`, `MultiServiceConfirmPage.tsx` and more, not just decorative/disabled elements)**: 2.54:1 against pure white — **fails WCAG AA even for large text** (needs 3:1) against the single most favorable background available anywhere in the app; degrades further (2.24:1, 1.84:1) against the tinted bubble backgrounds. This is the clearest, most unambiguous violation found — it fails the minimum bar everywhere, not just in a specific tinted context. For contrast: `#4b5563` and `#374151` (both also common) comfortably clear AA normal-text everywhere tested (7.2–10.3:1). Not fixed here — flagged with exact numbers and file-level usage sites so a fix can target `#9ca3af` first (clear, universal failure) and reconsider `#6b7280` specifically wherever it renders on a tinted/off-white background (the assistant's own message bubbles being the most common real-world case) rather than pure white.

#### Form validation edge cases (never systematically covered)

- [x] Extremely long input in every free-text field (customer name, personal message, review comment, notes) — does the UI truncate, wrap, overflow, or does the backend reject with a clean message? **Confirmed clean on the frontend rendering side; confirmed there is no backend length limit at all (accepts anything).** Live-tested on the gift-card checkout page's "Personal message" field: entered a 5,004-character string (`'X'.repeat(5000) + ' END'`) via a real form interaction and screenshotted the result — the textarea correctly wraps the text across many lines with no horizontal overflow, no truncation, no layout breakage; the field's box just grows taller to fit. Checked the backend side too: the customer-facing DTOs that accept these fields (`SubmitCustomerReviewDto.comment`, the gift-card purchase body, booking guest-name fields) have **no `@MaxLength` (or any length) validation at all** — confirmed via source read and a repo-wide grep for `MaxLength` across the whole backend (31 total usages, all confined to internal clinic-diagnostic-code/schedule/external-doctor modules, none in public-booking/gift-cards/reviews). The underlying DB columns match: `customers.name`, `reviews.customerName`, `bookings.notes` are all unbounded `character varying` and `reviews.comment` is `text` — no column-level truncation either. Net: the UI handles arbitrarily long input gracefully today (confirmed at 5,000 chars), but there is genuinely no length ceiling anywhere in the pipeline — a customer (or a scripted abuser) could submit an arbitrarily large string (megabytes) that would be silently accepted end-to-end with no rejection, which is more a latent data-quality/potential-abuse gap than a broken-UI bug. Not fixed here — flagged as a gap (add reasonable `@MaxLength` validation to these customer-facing DTOs) rather than a live-reproduced crash.
- [x] Unicode/emoji in names and comments (Armenian/Russian/Cyrillic characters specifically, given this app's actual locale set, plus emoji) — rendering and backend acceptance. **Confirmed clean.** Live-tested the same gift-card checkout's "Recipient name" field with a mixed string spanning all three of this app's actual locales plus emoji: `"Անի Հակոբյան 🎉 Иван Иванов 🎂✨"` (Armenian + emoji + Cyrillic + more emoji). Screenshotted the result: renders perfectly — correct Armenian and Cyrillic glyphs, correct emoji, no mojibake, no tofu/replacement-character boxes, no layout shift or truncation. Also triggered the real quote API call with this data present in the form and confirmed a clean `201 Created` response (no encoding-related rejection). Combined with the long-input finding above, free-text fields in this app handle both length and character-set edge cases correctly on the rendering side — the only real gap found across both items is the complete absence of backend length limits (already flagged above), not anything specific to unicode/emoji handling.
- [x] Email format edge cases — plus-addressing (`user+tag@domain.com`, already used throughout this session's test data), consecutive dots, missing TLD. **Booking endpoint validates correctly and consistently; gift-card endpoint has zero email format validation — a real, confirmed inconsistency.** Live-tested all 3 cases directly against `POST /public/{slug}/bookings` (`customer.email`, validated via `@IsEmail()` on `PublicCustomerDto` in `public-booking.dto.ts:26`): `test+tag@example.com` → **accepted**, real booking created (correct — plus-addressing is valid and this session's own test data uses it throughout); `test..name@example.com` (consecutive dots) → **cleanly rejected**, `400 "customer.email must be an email"`; `test@localhost` (missing TLD) → **cleanly rejected**, same clean message. All 3 outcomes are exactly correct, and the error messages are clean, specific, and customer-appropriate (not a raw validator.js internals dump). Cleaned up both real test bookings created via direct SQL afterward. **But found a real inconsistency while checking the gift-card purchase flow for comparison**: `POST /public/{slug}/gift-cards/quote` with `purchaserEmail: "test..bad@localhost"` (both consecutive dots AND missing TLD at once — the worst-case malformed input) → **accepted with a normal 201 quote response, zero validation**. Root cause, already documented under the earlier free-text-length finding: the gift-card purchase body isn't a class-validator DTO at all (`@Body() dto: { ... }` plain inline type in the controller), so NestJS's `ValidationPipe` never runs against it — no `@IsEmail()`, no length limits, nothing. In production this means a customer buying a gift card as a gift could enter a garbled recipient email and never find out until the delivery silently fails, unlike the booking flow which catches this immediately with a clear message. Same fix as task #235 (convert gift-card purchase body to a real class-validated DTO) would resolve this too.
- [x] Whitespace-only input in required fields — client-side `.trim()` checks exist in several places already read this session (`buildPayload` functions); confirm consistent trimming everywhere, not just some forms. **The consumer-app's own guest-checkout frontend correctly trims and rejects whitespace-only names; the backend has zero equivalent protection if that frontend gate is ever bypassed.** Traced the real guest-checkout submit path in `BookPage.tsx:submitBooking` (not just the button's `disabled` prop, which only gates on slot-selection/in-flight-state and turned out to be a red herring on its own) — the actual pre-submit guard is `validateGuestCheckoutContact` (`guest-booking.util.ts:19`): `if (!contact.name.trim()) return 'Enter your name.'`, plus a combined email-or-phone check. This correctly blocks whitespace-only names before any request is sent, with a clean, specific message — confirms the earlier-read `buildGiftCardPurchasePayload`/`canQuoteGiftCardPurchase` pattern (checking `.trim()` before allowing a quote) is consistently applied, at least across these two forms' client-side gates. **But live-tested bypassing the frontend entirely** (direct `POST /public/{slug}/bookings` call with `customer: { name: "     " (5 spaces), email: "...", phone: "..." }`) — the backend **accepted it and created a real booking** with a customer name that is, and will forever remain, invisible whitespace: no `@IsNotEmpty()`/trim-check anywhere in `PublicCustomerDto.name`'s validation (`@IsString()` alone permits any string, including one that's all whitespace). Cleaned up the test booking via direct SQL afterward. **Net finding**: the frontend does the right thing consistently in the two forms checked, but there is no server-side backstop at all — this is a real defense-in-depth gap, not a live customer-facing bug through the normal UI (a customer using the real app cannot currently trigger this), but it means any other current or future API consumer (a different client, a script, a future frontend regression) could silently create bookings/records with blank-looking required names with no complaint from the server.

#### Analytics / consent depth

- [x] Full consent lifecycle: never-asked → granted → declined → re-asked (if it ever re-asks) — `readAnalyticsConsent()`/`declineConsumerAnalyticsConsent()` seen in the AI assistant file; confirm the actual event-recording endpoint (`recordAppAnalyticsEvents`, API-sweep-confirmed working) genuinely stops receiving events after decline, not just that the UI stops asking. **The consent lifecycle logic itself is correctly implemented and verified live end-to-end — but found something far more severe while confirming it: the entire app-analytics pipeline is dead code, never wired into the running app at all.** Traced the intended bootstrap: `AppAnalyticsBootstrap.tsx` owns the one-time consent-prompt UI (shows only when `readAnalyticsConsent() == null`, correctly never re-asks once a decision is stored either way — confirmed via full source read, there is no other code path anywhere that re-triggers the prompt) and calls `configureAppAnalytics()` to initialize the module-level `context` that every `track()` call requires. A second path, `useSalonAppAnalytics` hook, also calls `configureAppAnalytics()` per-salon-visit. **Neither is referenced anywhere else in the codebase** — confirmed via exhaustive grep across every `.tsx` file including `App.tsx` itself: zero renders of `<AppAnalyticsBootstrap />`, zero calls to `useSalonAppAnalytics(...)`. Since `trackAppAnalyticsEvent`'s only gate is `if (!context || !consentGranted) return;` and `context` is set *exclusively* inside these two orphaned call sites, `context` never becomes non-null in the real running app — meaning **every `track(...)` call anywhere in the consumer-app (dozens of call sites: `signed_in`, `completed_booking`, `referral_accepted`, `app_opened`, etc.) is a silent, permanent no-op**, and the consent prompt itself never once renders to a real customer. Confirmed empirically, not just by static tracing: checked network history for `POST /events/app` across this entire multi-hour testing session (dozens of page loads, sign-ins, bookings, gift-card purchases) — **zero requests, ever**, until I manually simulated the missing bootstrap myself. **Once manually wired up via direct module calls (to test the logic itself, since it can't be reached any other way)**, the lifecycle behaves exactly correctly: a `track()` call before any consent decision is silently discarded (not queued for later); granting consent correctly flushes and sends events (confirmed via 2 real `POST /events/app` → `200`, `{recorded:1,skipped:0}` each); queuing 3 more events then calling `declineConsumerAnalyticsConsent()` *before* the 5-second flush timer fired, then waiting 6+ seconds past that window — produced **zero** further network requests, confirming decline correctly and permanently halts both already-queued-but-unflushed events and any new `track()` calls after it, with no race condition. So the actual answer to this checklist's core question is: the endpoint doesn't need to "stop receiving events after decline" in production today, because it never receives any events at all, from any consent state, because the pipeline was never connected. Also confirmed no manual "review/change your analytics choice" entry point exists anywhere in Account/Privacy settings (unlike the granular push-notification toggles that page does have) — even if the pipeline were wired up, a customer who declines has no way to reconsider short of clearing app storage. Not fixed here — this needs an actual product decision (mount `<AppAnalyticsBootstrap />` somewhere in `App.tsx`'s tree, and call `useSalonAppAnalytics` from wherever salon pages mount) plus ideally a settings entry point, not a quick patch.
- [x] Anonymous ID (`getOrCreateAnonId`) persistence and reset — does it survive app reinstall (it shouldn't, if tied to app storage) vs. survive a logout/login cycle (it should)? **Confirmed correct on both counts.** `getOrCreateAnonId()` (`app-analytics.ts:141`) is a plain `localStorage`-backed value (`app-analytics-anon-id` key) with no other persistence mechanism (no Keychain/Keystore, no server-side device registration) — confirmed via full source read. Live-tested the logout/login half directly: captured the anon ID, called the real `clearCustomerSession('gevgas-operations-7c299253')` (the actual sign-out function), confirmed the anon ID is **unchanged** afterward, then called the real `setCustomerSession(...)` (sign back in) and confirmed it's **still the same value** — because sign-out/sign-in only ever touch the `consumer_token_{slug}`/`consumer_profile_{slug}` keys, never `app-analytics-anon-id`, confirmed via source read of `customer-auth.ts`. Correct — this ID is meant to track the device/install, not the authenticated identity, so it should (and does) outlive any number of sign-in/out cycles. For app-reinstall: not literally testable without a real device reinstall, but confirmed by architecture rather than assumption — a Capacitor app's `localStorage` is backed by the OS's per-app sandboxed WebView storage (WKWebView on iOS, the Android WebView data directory), which is unconditionally wiped by the OS on uninstall; nothing in this code writes the anon ID anywhere else (no native Keychain/Keystore bridge, no server-issued device ID persisted independently), so a reinstall would deterministically produce a fresh ID — the correct, expected behavior.

#### Discovery / multi-salon (WelcomePage, recent salons)

- [x] `loadRecentSalons()` — visit 2+ different salons, confirm the recent-salons list populates correctly, in the right order (most-recent-first?), and that this list is what gets passed into AI assistant context (`recentSalons` field, already noted in the AI assistant plan) for cross-salon queries. **Population is correct; ordering has a real, reproducible bug in one specific scenario.** `rememberSalon()`/`rememberBookedSalon()` (`consumer-app/src/lib/recent-salons.ts:49-71`) fire from `useTenantStore.setProfile()` (`stores/tenant-store.ts:22`, on every tenant-profile load — i.e. every salon visit) and from `BookPage.tsx:275` (on a completed booking). Live-tested via direct module injection (`import('/src/lib/recent-salons.ts')`, since this is pure storage logic uninvolved with the flaky Ionic UI): visiting salon A then B populates `loadRecentSalons()` as `[B, A]` and `buildWelcomeSalonSections().recent` (used by `WelcomePage.tsx`) agrees — both most-recent-first, correct. **Bug**: `salonRecencyTimestamp()` (`recent-salons.ts:41-43`) computes recency as `lastBookedAt ?? visitedAt` — once a salon has ever been booked, its `lastBookedAt` permanently wins over any *later* plain revisit's `visitedAt`. Reproduced: visited A, booked A (`lastBookedAt=t2`), visited B (`visitedAt=t3`, t3>t2), then revisited A again (`visitedAt=t4`, t4>t3, but `lastBookedAt` stays t2) — `WelcomePage`'s `sections.recent` order came back `[B, A]` (B ranked above A) even though A was the salon the user *just* opened, because A's stale `lastBookedAt` (t2) loses to B's `visitedAt` (t3). Meanwhile the raw storage array (`loadRecentSalons()`, unsorted, LRU-by-touch) correctly had `[A, B]` — meaning **`ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx:191`'s `recentSalons` context field (which maps `loadRecentSalons()` directly, with no sort) can disagree with what `WelcomePage` visually shows as "recent"** for the same underlying data, depending on booking history. Net effect: once you've ever booked with a salon, simply reopening it later doesn't bump it back to the top of the Welcome page's recent list — a stale "last booked" timestamp outranks a fresh visit. Not fixed here (a one-line semantic call on whether "most recently booked" or "most recently touched at all" should win — a product decision, not a bug that has one obviously-correct fix). Filed as a task.
- [x] Switching between salons — does customer auth/session correctly scope per-salon (already implied by `consumer_token_${slug}` storage keys seen early this session), with no session bleed between two different businesses open in sequence. **Confirmed correct**, verified two ways. (1) Code: every consumer-app call site that reads a session token (`getCustomerToken(slug)` in `customer-auth.ts:14`) is grepped and confirmed to always pass the *currently-routed* `slug` param — no module-level cached "current customer" variable anywhere; storage keys are `consumer_token_${slug}`/`consumer_profile_${slug}`, fully namespaced per business. (2) Live UI test using the app's real flow (not just storage inspection): signed in as "Alice Test" at `gevgas-operations-7c299253` (via `setCustomerSession`, since real sign-in needs live Google OAuth), navigated to a second real business `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8`'s Account page — correctly showed "Sign in to see appointments and subscriptions at Pollin Clinic" with **no bleed** of the Alice session. Used the app's own "Switch salon" screen (`buildRememberedTenants()`, `customer-auth.ts:149`) to jump back to GevGas — correctly still showed "Alice Test" signed in, and the salon-switcher list correctly showed Pollin Clinic as "Current salon" (not signed in) alongside "Alice Test · Signed in · Visited today" for GevGas, in the same list. No session bleed in either direction.

  Note: while testing this, hit a red herring worth recording — directly loading a bare `/gevgas-operations-7c299253` URL (no `/s/` prefix) renders a completely blank page with zero console errors, because the app's real route table (`App.tsx:51-103`) is entirely under an `/s/:slug/...` prefix with no bare-slug catch-all. This is **not an app bug**, just an easy trap when constructing consumer-app URLs by hand outside the app's own links (which always correctly emit the `/s/` prefix, confirmed via the "Switch salon" and salon-code-entry flows both landing on valid `/s/:slug/home` URLs).

#### App version gate (partially known, never fully cased)

- [x] Optional update available (`updateRequired: false` but a newer version exists) — does the app show a dismissible nudge rather than the full block already confirmed for `updateRequired: true`? **Confirmed correct.** Live-tested `evaluateMobileAppGate`/`shouldShowUpdateNudge` (`consumer-app/src/lib/app-version-gate.util.ts`) via direct module injection with `{minSupportedVersion:'1.0.0', latestVersion:'1.2.0', updateRequired:false}` and `currentVersion:'1.1.0'`: `evaluateMobileAppGate` → `{blocked:false}` and `shouldShowUpdateNudge` → `true`. Traced the render path (`AppVersionGate.tsx:23-69`): when `blocked` is falsy it renders `children` normally plus an `AppUpdateNudgeBanner` with an `onDismiss` handler — a dismissible banner, not the full-screen `role="dialog"` block used for the `updateRequired`/`killSwitch` cases. Correct behavior, matches the checklist's expectation exactly.
- [x] Nudge dismissal persistence (`dismissConsumerAppUpdateNudge`, seen as an AI-assistant client-action) — confirm dismissing doesn't re-nudge every single app open, only on some reasonable cadence. **Mostly correct, with one caveat worth flagging.** `dismissUpdateNudge(key)` (`app-version-gate.util.ts:80-83`) writes to `sessionStorage`, not `localStorage`, keyed by `app-update-nudge:{surface}:{latestVersion}` (`buildUpdateNudgeDismissKey`). Live-verified: dismissing sets `sessionStorage` (confirmed `localStorage.getItem(key)` stayed `null`), and a subsequent `shouldShowUpdateNudge` call with the same key correctly returns `false` — so within one continuous app session, dismissing genuinely does not re-nudge, and keying by `latestVersion` correctly means a *new* release (new `latestVersion`) produces a new key and re-nudges as it should, rather than being suppressed forever by a stale dismissal. The caveat: because this is `sessionStorage` rather than a persisted timestamp/cadence in `localStorage`, dismissal does **not** survive a genuine app-process relaunch — for a Capacitor native app, `sessionStorage` lives only as long as the WebView instance; once iOS/Android evicts the app from memory (very common — backgrounded apps get killed under memory pressure, or after a device restart) and the user reopens it, the WebView is recreated and the nudge reappears even though nothing about the version changed. So "some reasonable cadence" is true only for "same continuous session," not "same day" or "same app version" as a user would likely expect from tapping "dismiss." Not fixed here — this is a legitimate product/UX gap (no test file existed for this module at all prior to this pass, confirming it was genuinely never cased), filed as a task.
- [x] Exact boundary condition — a version exactly equal to `minSupportedVersion` (not less than) — off-by-one risk in the comparison logic. **Confirmed correct, no off-by-one.** Live-tested `isVersionBelowMinimum('2.0.0', '2.0.0')` → `false` (equal versions are correctly NOT flagged as below minimum, so a version exactly at the floor is allowed through, not blocked) and `evaluateMobileAppGate` with `currentVersion === minSupportedVersion === latestVersion` → `{blocked:false}`. Also spot-checked adjacent boundaries: `isVersionBelowMinimum('2.0.0', '2.0.1')` → `true` (one patch below correctly caught) and `isVersionBelowMinimum('2.0.1', '2.0.0')` → `false` (one patch above correctly not flagged). `compareSemver`'s component-wise loop (`app-version-gate.util.ts:10-19`) returns `0` for a fully-equal triple, and `isVersionBelowMinimum` only flags `cmp < 0`, so equality is unambiguously treated as "meets the minimum," which is the semantically correct interpretation of "minimum supported version."

## consumer-ai-cmd-e2e-plan.1 — Customer-surface AI commands full test plan, A to Z (planning pass)

Planning pass only, per explicit request — build the plan first, execute in later turns. Scope: every AI intent reachable by a **customer** (a real signed-in consumer-app/web user) or an **anonymous public visitor** (the `/book/[slug]` web flow or a guest with no account) — not dashboard-only or provider-mobile-only intents. Grounded in a full registry inventory (not guessed): the master registry (`ai-command-registry.build.ts`, `INTENT_BINDING_SEEDS`/`LEGACY_CORE_BINDINGS`) is **data-driven** — `CUSTOMER_INTENTS`/`PUBLIC_INTENTS`/`*_MUTATING_INTENTS` are computed from seed bindings, not a hand-maintained list — so the authoritative per-intent surface/mutating-status source for any single test is `resolveIntentSurfaces(id)` / the seed block itself, not this document's summary.

**Architecture notes that shape how this whole plan must be executed (read before testing anything):**
1. **Two endpoints, one shared classifier core.** Signed-in customers hit `CustomerAiCommandService` (native intents) which **delegates** 14 discovery/anonymous-booking intents (`PUBLIC_ONLY_ASSISTANT_ACTIONS` — `list_providers`, `list_services`, `find_services_under_budget`, `find_evening_weekend_slots`, `check_availability`, `explain_provider_availability`, `recommend_specialists`, `business_info`, `book_appointment`, `booking_help`, `preview_multi_service_cart`, `list_public_promotions`, `list_provider_reviews`, `suggest_package_block`) into `PublicBookingAssistantService.chat()`. Anonymous visitors hit `POST /public/:slug/assistant` (`assistantMode: 'guide'|'act'`) directly — no separate REST route per intent, one chat endpoint for everything.
2. **No swipe-to-confirm on customer/public surfaces** — that's a dashboard/provider-only UI convention. The **only** customer intent with an explicit two-turn confirm is `cancel_all_upcoming_bookings`: first call returns `requiresConfirmation: true` + a preview list of what would be cancelled; the follow-up call must carry `params.confirm === true` to actually execute. Every other mutating customer intent (including `cancel_my_booking`) executes on a single classified turn — **this is itself the highest-priority thing to test**: does a single ambiguous or ordinary-sounding sentence ever accidentally fire an irreversible mutation with zero safety net?
3. **No ReAct/LLM-based replanning on customer or public surfaces.** `ReactBookingAgentService`/`BookingCommandGraphService` are wired only into the **dashboard** controller (`JwtAuthGuard`-gated `ai-command.controller.ts`) — confirmed via import grep that neither `customer-ai-command.service.ts` nor `public-booking-assistant.service.ts` reference them. All customer/public ambiguity resolution is deterministic rule-based `rescueIntent()` — do not expect a compound/ambiguous prompt to get "figured out" via multi-step LLM reasoning the way a dashboard prompt might; a prompt the deterministic rescue can't match will fall to `unknown`, not a smarter fallback.
4. **Guest-token intents bypass JWT auth entirely.** `bookings/manage*` REST endpoints (`GET bookings/manage`, `POST bookings/manage/cancel`/`reschedule`/`package/cancel`/`package/reschedule`) have **no** `@UseGuards` — they authenticate purely via `{bookingId, token}`. Contrast `/me/bookings/:id/...` endpoints, which require `PublicCustomerAuthGuard`. The AI-side guest intents (`explain_manage_booking_context`, `cancel_booking_with_token`, `reschedule_booking_with_token`, `cancel_package_visit_with_token`, `reschedule_package_visit_with_token`, plus the `guest_manage_visit`/`guest_book_and_manage`/`guest_pay_cash_manage` compounds) must be tested **without any Authorization header** — only the booking's own manage-link token.
5. **Shared vs customer-only rescue routing.** Per `CUSTOMER_PUBLIC_RESCUE_ROUTING` (`ai-capability.matrix.ts:458-487`): "shared discovery" prompts (budget search, provider ranking, OR-style availability) are documented and expected to rescue identically whether sent to the anonymous `/public/:slug/assistant` endpoint or the signed-in customer endpoint. "Customer-only" domains (account, payments, packages, clinic self-service, adoption/rewards) are wired to rescue **only** on the customer path — sending an account/payment/cancel prompt to the anonymous public endpoint should never rescue or execute; if it does, that's a real security-boundary bug, not a feature.
6. **Confirmed classifier-fixture gaps to prioritize** (from `ai-registry-nl-fixture-coverage.build.ts` cross-reference, not naive grepping — some domains bundle multiple intents' HY/RU fixtures into one shared file, so a missing standalone file ≠ zero coverage; verify via the repo's own coverage tool before concluding a gap is real): **`cancel_my_booking`** (15 EN prompts, **0 HY / 0 RU**), **`reschedule_my_booking`** (~15 EN, **0 HY / 0 RU**), **`reschedule_package_lines`** (no multilingual file found), **`get_manage_link`** (only 1 HY + 1 RU total — thin), **`suggest_package_block`** (5 EN, no multilingual), **`list_provider_reviews`** (4 EN, no multilingual). These are the two highest-traffic *mutating* booking-lifecycle intents (cancel/reschedule) with a confirmed zero-multilingual gap — start here.
7. **Test mechanics**: drive prompts through the real UI (`ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx` in `consumer-app`, or the `/book/[slug]` web equivalent) wherever possible so classification + dispatch + UI rendering are all exercised together, not just the raw API; fall back to direct `POST /public/:slug/assistant` curl calls only for surface-boundary/security tests where the UI itself would prevent constructing the request (e.g. testing an account intent with no session).

- [x] `find_services_under_budget` — a budget with 0 matches, a budget matching everything, non-numeric/garbled budget phrasing ("under a hundred bucks-ish"). **0-match and match-everything cases are clean; the fuzzy-phrasing case surfaced a real, reproducible classifier hallucination.** Live-tested against `gevgas-operations-7c299253` (15 services, $5–$333): "under $1" → 0 matches, correctly returns `"Nothing under $1.\n\nClosest options:"` plus the 3 cheapest services (`buildBudgetListServicesNoMatchSummary`, `.slice(0, 3)`); "under $10000" → correctly lists all 15 services, no special-casing needed since nothing breaks by listing everything. "under a hundred bucks-ish" → `maxPrice` correctly resolved to `100` — confirmed via source (`ai-budget-service-discovery.util.ts`) this is accidental-but-correct: the two-word `BUDGET_WORD_AMOUNT_PATTERN` requires the literal word `dollars` (not `bucks`) so it doesn't match, but `BUDGET_WORD_BUCKS_PATTERN` (`/\b([a-z]+)\s+bucks?\b/i`) then captures just `hundred` (the word immediately before "bucks"), and `parseWordAmount('hundred')` resolves via `WORD_NUMBER_MAP` to 100 — right answer, fragile mechanism. **The real finding**: truly non-numeric budget phrasing with no resolvable word-number at all does not fail safe — it's inconsistent and sometimes fabricates a number. Tested three more phrasings with no explicit number and no `WORD_NUMBER_MAP` word: "under a reasonable amount" deterministically resolved `maxPrice: 50` on 3 repeated calls (traced the entire deterministic `extractMaxPriceFromBudgetPrompt` regex chain by hand — none of its ~15 branches, including the word-ceiling one which only captures the single word "a" and fails `parseWordAmount`, can produce 50 for this input — so the 50 is coming from the live LLM classifier's own entity extraction, not the deterministic rescue util); "give me something cheap-ish" also produced a fabricated `maxPrice: 50`; "I don't want to spend too much" instead came back with `maxPrice: null` and gracefully fell back to listing the unfiltered catalog (safe, but arguably not what a "budget" intent should do either); "keep it within my means" failed classification entirely (`action: unknown`, "I didn't fully understand that"). So the live classifier's handling of genuinely non-numeric budget language is inconsistent across three different failure modes (silently invent a plausible-sounding number and filter by it without disclosing the guess; correctly detect no number and show everything unfiltered; or give up entirely) depending on phrasing, not a single deterministic behavior. The middle case (no filter applied) is safe; the first case (inventing $50 and silently filtering) is the concerning one — a customer could be shown a narrower list than they'd actually accept, based on a number they never said, with no indication the assistant guessed. Filed as a task.

Instead tested the other two sub-items directly against the real booking-creation endpoint (`POST /public/:slug/bookings`), since that's the actual transaction any successful `book_appointment` execution — AI-driven or manual checkout — ultimately goes through, and it's the layer where race-safety and input validation actually live. **Race condition**: booked a specific real slot (Gevorg, Swedish massage, 30/07/2026 09:00) successfully (`201`, real booking created), then immediately attempted to book the *exact same* slot again for a different customer — correctly rejected with a clean `409 {"message":"That time is already booked.   **e2e-bug.75 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: every mutating self-service-booking intent whose natural phrasing mentions "my booking/appointment/visit" (at minimum `cancel_my_booking`, `reschedule_my_booking`, `cancel_all_upcoming_bookings`, `cancel_package_visit_self`, `reschedule_package_visit_self`, `confirm_my_booking_details`, `add_booking_to_calendar`) — plus `cancel_my_subscription` and `start_pre_visit_intake` — got silently overridden to read-only `my_appointments` / `my_subscriptions` by the customer-CRM rescue pass, even when the LLM classified it correctly.

**Root-cause discussion (word-boundary collision, applies to this bug + e2e-bug.76 + the `start_pre_visit_intake` victim found in Section G)**: the deeper reason these action-exclusion patches keep being necessary is that `\bvisits?\b`-style regexes can't distinguish "cancel my **visit**" from "pre-**visit** intake" — JS regex `\b` treats hyphens as word boundaries identical to spaces, so any compound term (`pre-visit`, `walk-in`, `no-show`, `follow-up`, `check-in`) collides with a bare word check. Confirmed via code read: the codebase's only existing "prompt normalization" (`AiPromptNormalizationService.normalizeForClassifier()`) exclusively does language/multilingual detection, not lexical/compound-word normalization — there is no shared tokenizer. Discussed 2 fix directions with the user (holding both for the later fix pass, not implemented this session): **(B, recommended first pass)** a single shared `maskDomainCompounds(prompt)` helper (a small fixed list of known compound terms — `pre-visit`, `walk-in`, `no-show`, `follow-up`, `check-in`, `check-out` — rewritten to underscore-joined tokens before any `isXPrompt()` regex runs) added to the existing normalization service, replacing the current whack-a-mole of per-function action-exclusion patches; **(C, longer-term)** widen the already-built embedding-based `AiSemanticIntentService` semantic-anchor matcher (currently only invoked when LLM confidence is low) to arbitrate this class of regex-vs-meaning collision generally, since embeddings don't have the word-boundary blind spot at all. Neither guarantees zero false positives forever — only reduces this specific recurring bug class.

- [x] `cancel_package_visit_self` [M], `reschedule_package_visit_self` [M], `reschedule_package_lines` [M] (no multilingual fixtures either) — cancel one line of a multi-line package visit vs. the whole visit (does the natural-language classifier distinguish "cancel my massage" from "cancel my whole package"?) **The question turns out to be moot for a more fundamental reason: none of these 3 intents can act on a single line within a visit at all — it's an architectural "whole visit only" constraint, not a classifier gap.** Traced all 3 down to their shared underlying service methods in full: `cancel_package_visit_self` → `cancelPackageVisitInternal` (`public-customer-booking.service.ts:598-650`) loads *every* booking in the visit block (`loadPackageVisitBookings`), checks a whole-visit policy literally named `canCancelAll`, and — if allowed — loops through and cancels **every** active-status booking in that visit; there is no parameter anywhere in this intent (`bookingId`/`packageName`/`visitIndex` — never a per-service target) that could even express "just the massage line." So even a perfect classifier that correctly extracted "the customer means just the massage service" would have nowhere to put that information — the handler and the service method beneath it only understand "this whole visit, yes or no." `reschedule_package_visit_self` → `reschedulePackageVisitInternal` (line 664-714) is stricter still: it hard-rejects unless `dto.lines.length === active.length` (`"Provide a new time for each appointment in this package visit"`) — every active line must get an explicit new time in the same call. The "lines[] auto-build" feature (task #14, already shipped earlier this session) doesn't provide selective per-line control either — `buildPackageVisitLinesFromTarget` (confirmed via source) anchors the **entire visit** to one new target start time and recomputes each service's back-to-back slot sequentially from that anchor, i.e. it auto-fills the required lines array by shifting the whole block uniformly, not by preserving some lines' original times while moving just one. `reschedule_package_lines` operates one level up — its "lines" are different *visit numbers* within a recurring package schedule (visit 1, visit 2, visit 3...), each one moved to a new day via the same whole-visit-shift mechanism per visit; it's not about services within a single visit either. **Net finding**: a customer who packages multiple services into one visit (e.g. massage + facial, this business's own max is 5 services/visit) has no way — via AI chat or, per this trace, via the underlying API at all — to cancel or reschedule just one of those services while keeping the others; any action targeting the visit necessarily affects every service booked within it. Filed as a task, framed as a product-level capability gap rather than a classifier bug, since fixing the classifier alone couldn't resolve it.

For the 3 compounds: `guest_manage_visit`'s own trigger guard (`isGuestContext`, `ai-guest-manage-visit-compound.util.ts:41-48`) explicitly returns `false` — refusing to even decompose into the guest compound — whenever `params.sessionCustomerId || params.customerId` is present, so a signed-in customer's cancel/reschedule request correctly never enters the guest-lookup path at all and instead falls through to the normal session-based intent. `guest_book_and_manage`/`guest_pay_cash_manage` have no equivalent session guard, but their trigger phrasing requires an explicit "as guest"/"without account" cue in the prompt — a signed-in customer would only reach them by literally asking to check out as a guest, which is a deliberate, correct override of their own session (not an accidental fallback), consistent with how guest checkout is allowed to bypass an existing account by design.

  **e2e-bug.89 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: the `cancel_and_rebook` compound (and by extension any compound whose steps include `cancel_my_booking`) failed at the cancellation step with "No upcoming booking found to cancel," even though the test account had 2 real, confirmed upcoming bookings (one of them the exact service named in the prompt). Reproduced live: `"cancel my facemassage appointment and book the next available slot instead"` → `{"action":"compound_intent","summary":"Stopped at step 1 (cancel_my_booking): No upcoming booking found to cancel."}` — confirmed immediately before and after via a plain `"list my appointments"` call on the same session returning "You have 2 upcoming appointment(s)." **This is a materially different bug from e2e-bug.75, not a duplicate**: compound sub-steps are dispatched directly by action name (confirmed via reading `AiCommandService.executeCompoundIntents()`, `ai-command.service.ts:2909+`), completely bypassing the classifier-rescue chain where `isMyAppointmentsPrompt()` lives — so this proves the `cancel_my_booking` *handler itself*, once actually reached, has its own separate booking-lookup defect, not merely a routing problem. **Partial root-cause lead, not fully confirmed this pass**: read `command-completion.pipeline.service.ts`'s `mergeSessionContext()` (called from `executeCompoundIntents` to thread session context into each compound sub-step) and found its `SESSION_INHERIT_KEYS` allow-list (lines 40-78, ~30 entries covering `serviceName`, `employeeName`, `packageId`, etc.) **does not include `sessionCustomerId` or `customerId` at all** — meaning if customer identity for a compound step relies on this same generic merge mechanism (not yet confirmed either way — the response's specific "no booking found" wording rather than a "sign in" message suggests identity *was* resolved via some other path, so this may be a red herring rather than the root cause), it would never be threaded through. **This needs dedicated tracing in the fix pass** (add temporary logging to `handleCancelMyBookingLogic`'s booking-lookup query when invoked via the compound path vs. the standalone path, to see exactly what `businessId`/`customerId`/`serviceName` values it receives) rather than guessing further from static reads alone. **Real-world impact**: this is a 2nd, independent way the single highest-priority customer capability (cancelling a booking) fails — even a customer whose prompt is clean enough to avoid e2e-bug.75/76/77's classification traps entirely still cannot complete a cancel-and-rebook in one message.

### Closure
Compile all findings into a single closure entry here, following the established `e2e-bug.N` numbering (continuing from **e2e-bug.74**), with root-cause file:line citations and fix directions for each. Explicitly call out confirmed-clean areas and confirmed classifier-fixture gaps (Section N.6) separately from genuine functional/security bugs, and note any test-only mutations (bookings/subscriptions/gift cards cancelled, reviews submitted, etc.) that were reverted after testing.

- **e2e-bug.82** (expanded, now the 2nd-most pervasive defect found): at least **10 files / 13+ customer intents** — `refer_a_friend`, `share_salon_link`, `explain_rewards_wallet`, `claim_referral_code`, `claim_share_reward`, `update_my_profile`, `update_my_locale`, `list_provider_reviews`, `pick_provider_for_service`, `share_my_booking`, `switch_provider_same_time`, `rebook_last_appointment`, `submit_review_with_token` (guest-token variant), `submit_provider_review` — unconditionally fail with "Business not found." for every customer, on every business, because they read a `params.slug` the classifier never populates, instead of resolving it server-side from the already-available `businessId` like every correctly-implemented sibling handler does.
- **e2e-bug.83** — **Fixed** (see dedicated write-up). Originally: `claim_referral_code` unreachable — `isApplyGiftCardCodePrompt()` matched "redeem" + bare "code", so "redeem referral code X" became `apply_gift_card_code`.
- **e2e-bug.84** — **Fixed** (see dedicated write-up). Originally: `privacy_delete` had no confirmation — a single sentence anonymized PII immediately.
- **e2e-bug.85**: `explain_rtl_layout` never knows the customer's real locale (hardcodes "EN" regardless of what's requested) — another `params.X` field the classifier never populates, silently defaulting instead of erroring.
- **e2e-bug.86**: `explain_rtl_layout`'s customer-facing reply leaks a raw internal CSS filename (`adoption-a11y.css`) baked directly into the response text.
- **e2e-bug.87** (**the single most severe finding of the entire pass**) — **Fixed.** A large fraction of the hy-locale (Armenian) guide/help content shown across nearly the whole customer+public guide corpus was garbled, illegible mixed-script text (Armenian + Latin transliteration + stray Cyrillic within single words) — confirmed via direct read of the 156-line source file (`guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json`), with the parallel ru-locale file completely correct for the same flows, and reproduced independently with an unrelated prompt. This guide content is attached to a large fraction of assistant responses site-wide, meaning any real Armenian-speaking customer had likely been shown broken, unprofessional text every time the assistant needed to give step-by-step guidance. Fully re-translated all 20 affected flows in that file plus a second, previously-unknown-affected sibling file (`consumer-app/src/assets/guide-flows-i18n.json`, which the native "Help & guide" UI reads directly); regenerated the derived snapshot; the pre-existing 81-test locale-parity spec passes; live-reconfirmed clean via both original repro paths (native GuidePage in real hy locale, and the AI chat's post-failure guide-fallback with a garbled prompt). Full details above.
- **e2e-bug.89**: the `cancel_and_rebook` compound fails at its cancellation step with "No upcoming booking found to cancel" despite 2 real bookings existing — a **materially different bug from e2e-bug.75**, since compound sub-steps dispatch directly by action name and completely bypass the classifier-rescue chain where e2e-bug.75 lives. — **Fixed** (see Fix log): root cause was `extractServiceNameFromPrompt` inventing `serviceName: "next available"` from the book-half phrase, not missing `sessionCustomerId`.

**Net effect**: as of this pass, the entire cancellation/reschedule surface across bookings AND subscriptions, the entire gift-card purchase funnel, the entire referral/sharing feature batch, `update_my_profile`/`update_my_locale`/several review-and-provider-selection intents, AND the entire hy-locale guide/help experience — cannot be completed or trusted via natural-language conversation on the live dev environment (24+ distinct prompts tried across 15+ intents for the mutation-blocking bugs, 0 successful executions) — plus one intent (`privacy_delete`) that executes *too* easily, with no safety gate at all, and one static content file that's badly broken for an entire supported language. e2e-bug.75/76/77/82/83/87 are deterministic and 100% reproducible (not LLM temperature noise); e2e-bug.78 and half of e2e-bug.80 (the `get_gift_card_quote` half) are the exceptions where the root cause sits in LLM judgment rather than a hard code/regex/data defect.

## web-booking-e2e-plan.1 — Public booking web app (`frontend`'s `/book/[slug]/*`), full test plan A-Z, including all AI commands on this surface

Planning pass — grounded in a real inventory before execution. `frontend` (Next.js web) is a single codebase bundling three distinct surfaces (staff/admin dashboard, this public booking web app, and a web provider view); this plan covers **only** the public booking web app, i.e. everything under `/book/[slug]/*`, **including its AI assistant widget**. This is a **separate implementation** from `consumer-app` (the native mobile app already fully tested this session) — same backend, but its own React pages and its own dedicated API client (`frontend/src/lib/public-api.ts`, 1496 lines, confirmed 78 real endpoint-calling functions via `grep '^export function\|^export async function'`), so it is expected to have its own distinct bugs, not a re-run of already-found ones. The AI backend logic itself was already exhaustively tested this session (`consumer-ai-cmd-e2e-plan.1`, 31 bugs, e2e-bug.75-105) — Sections F onward below deliberately reuse that plan's intent groupings, but the goal here is different: does driving the **same intents through this specific web UI** surface *new*, UI-layer bugs (widget rendering, session/history handling, navigate-target correctness, this-surface-specific param wiring) on top of the already-known backend defects, and do the already-known backend defects reproduce identically here or does the web UI's own code path diverge (better or worse)? Never tested this session until now.

### e2e-bug.101 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — found and fixed a real, narrower gap; closing out the "mention-only" status

Re-verified from scratch rather than trusting the "largely fixed" framing at face value. Confirmed live against the real backend (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`) that `most_expensive`/`cheapest` extraction is genuinely symmetric and no longer treats the rank phrase as a literal service name — that part of the original write-up holds. But the write-up's own caveat ("category not in this catalog" for `styling`) turned out to be only half-true, and digging into *why* surfaced a real, narrowly-scoped bug worth fixing.

**Investigated whether "facial"/"styling" are genuinely unrecognized vocabulary or just absent from this business's catalog.** Read `ai-service-rank-discovery.util.ts`'s category-extraction regex (`RANK_SERVICE_CATEGORY_PATTERN`) — it captures *any* word following a rank adjective, with no closed vocabulary list; "facial" and "styling" both extract cleanly (already covered by `ai-e2e101-service-rank-asymmetric.util.spec.ts`). So the failure has to be downstream, at catalog matching.

- **"facial" — confirmed a genuine catalog-data gap, not a bug.** Queried the real DB directly: no business anywhere in this dev database has a service named or categorized "facial" (this business's closest matches are "Face Pilling"/"Face Plasma" — a fuzzy-matching gap arguably, but a different, broader issue than e2e-bug.101's rank-vocabulary scope, and not fixed here).
- **"styling" — found a real, narrow bug.** This business *does* have a Hair Care service literally named "hairstyle" (confirmed via DB query and live `curl`: `"What's the cheapest hairstyle?"` → succeeds, `$15`). But `"What is the most expensive styling?"` / `"cheapest styling"` still failed — because the rank module's `RANK_SERVICE_CATEGORY_ALIASES` map (which already had `cut`/`cuts`/`trim` → `haircut`, established for e2e-bug.199) never included `style`/`styles`/`styling`. The bare word never got a chance to reach the haircut↔hairstyle synonym expansion that `filterServicesByCategory` already applies to the word `haircut`.

**Fix**: added `style: 'haircut'`, `styles: 'haircut'`, `styling: 'haircut'` to `RANK_SERVICE_CATEGORY_ALIASES` in [`ai-service-rank-discovery.util.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-service-rank-discovery.util.ts) — same pattern as the existing `cut`/`cuts`/`trim` entries, reusing the already-established haircut/hairstyle synonym expansion rather than adding a new one.

**Verification**:
1. Live re-test on the real backend, both rank directions: `"most expensive styling"` and `"cheapest styling"` now both succeed → real `hairstyle` service, $15. `"most premium style"` (singular) and `"most expensive trim"`/`"cheapest cut"` (regression check on the pre-existing aliases) all still resolve correctly too.
2. New test block in `ai-e2e101-service-rank-asymmetric.util.spec.ts` covering `style`/`styles`/`styling` for both rank directions plus a `cut`/`trim` regression check.
3. Fixing the extraction correctly changed 5 existing test expectations that had literally asserted the un-aliased `'styling'` string as the "correct" output (`ai-e2e101-service-rank-asymmetric.fixtures.ts`, `ai-service-catalog-rank.fixtures.ts`, `ai-service-discovery.integration.spec.ts` ×2 via one shared fixture id) — updated all 5 to expect `'haircut'`, matching the corrected behavior. Confirmed via `git stash` diff on every affected test file that these were the *only* net-new differences from baseline (ran the full surrounding fixture/spec cluster — 823 tests — before and after; identical failing-test set both times except these 5, which now match the fix).
4. `tsc --noEmit` — zero new errors vs. baseline (confirmed via the same before/after `git stash` comparison).

**"facial" remains open** — not a rank-vocabulary bug, and out of scope here (would need either seeded facial-service test data to prove/disprove a matching gap, or a broader fuzzy-match improvement for "facial" ↔ "Face Pilling"/"Face Plasma"-style catalog naming, which is a different class of fix than this bug's rank-extraction scope).

- [x] **Priority: re-verify e2e-bug.96 (the unauthenticated cross-customer IDOR on `confirm_my_booking_details`)** specifically through this web UI's own request-building code — does the web app ever construct a request shaped like the raw curl exploit (a bare `context.bookingId` with no session), or does its own client code happen to avoid this attack shape entirely? This matters for real-world exploitability assessment, not just backend correctness.

  **Verdict (live 2026-07-28, `frontend` @ `:3002`, slug `gevgas-operations-7c299253`, victim booking `fbb0aa49-…`, fully anonymous):** the **real client does construct the IDOR-shaped request** whenever the URL carries `?bookingId=` — it does **not** avoid the attack shape. Source: `extractPublicAssistantQueryContext` → `buildPublicAssistantPageContext` → every `sendPublicAssistantMessage` merges that into `context` ([public-booking-assistant-context.util.ts](frontend/src/lib/public-booking-assistant-context.util.ts), [public-booking-assistant.tsx](frontend/src/components/public-booking/public-booking-assistant.tsx)). Puppeteer intercepts:

  | Scenario | Client sends `context.bookingId`? | `manageToken` / session? | Reached `confirm_my_booking_details`? | PII leak? |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Home, free-text only (`confirm… booking ID <uuid>`) | No (id stays in prompt only) | No | No (`guide_user_flow`) | No |
  | Home `?bookingId=<victim>` | **Yes** | No | (guide mode often steers away) | No |
  | Manage `?bookingId=<victim>` (no token) | **Yes** | No | **Yes** (act/default) | **No** — `"Share the manage link…"` |
  | Manage `?bookingId=<victim>&token=garbage` | **Yes** | garbage only | **Yes** (API act-mode twin) | **No** — same deny |

  **Exploitability:** request construction via the real UI is **reachable** (paste/share a manage or home URL with a guessed/leaked `bookingId`, open the widget, ask to confirm). **Data exfil is not** — backend e2e-bug.128 / e2e-bug.96 fix still holds on this path. Earlier Section K note that “the client never includes `bookingId`” was true only for free-text-on-bare-home; it is **superseded** by URL-query threading (post e2e-bug.106). No new client bug filed — optional defense-in-depth would be to omit `bookingId` from assistant context unless a `token` is also present.

## e2e-bug.102 — a guest who types their bookingId/token as plain text (no pasted URL) gets silently misrouted, unlike one who pastes the manage-link URL — **Fixed**

This ticket was genuinely never investigated before — both prior mentions (`TODO.md` L1597, L2270) only ever flagged "e2e-bug.102's URL-vs-freetext distinction" as a planned question for a later pass; no findings were ever recorded. Investigated and root-caused from scratch, guru manual QA style, live against the real running backend.

**Reproduced live, twice, with a fake-but-realistic UUID + hex token (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`):**

| Phrasing | action | result |
|---|---|---|
| `"Please cancel my booking https://example.com/manage?bookingId=<uuid>&token=<hex>"` (pasted URL) | `cancel_booking_with_token` | **Correct** — `"Booking not found"` (right handler, credentials extracted, clean reject on a fake id) |
| `"Please cancel my booking. The booking id is <uuid> and the manage token is <hex>"` (same info, typed as plain text) | `compound_intent` | **Wrong** — silently fell into `guest_manage_visit`'s `get_manage_link` step, which then failed with `"No upcoming booking found for that email or phone"` — a completely different, misleading failure mode for a customer who gave the assistant everything it needed |
| `"What is this booking? The booking id is <uuid> and the manage token is <hex>"` (explain, same free-text style) | `confirm_my_booking_details` | **Wrong** — `"Share the manage link for this booking first, so I can look it up."`, ignoring the id+token already given in the same sentence |

Reproduced identically across the cancel and explain intents; not a one-off classifier fluke.

**Root cause, found by reading the actual code rather than guessing:** `ai-manage-booking-with-token.util.ts` already has a robust, deterministic rescue (`rescueManageBookingWithTokenIntent`) that re-routes *any* misclassified prompt to the correct `cancel_booking_with_token` / `reschedule_booking_with_token` / `explain_manage_booking_context` action, as long as it can detect valid-looking credentials in the prompt (`hasManageLinkCredentials`). But `extractManageLinkCredentialsFromPrompt` — the function that detection depends on — only ever matched the URL query-string shape (`[?&]bookingId=...`, `[?&]token=...`). A customer who typed the same two values as plain, clearly-labelled text (copied out of an email body, read aloud, dictated via voice input, or simply not comfortable pasting a raw URL) produced zero matches, so the rescue never fired and whatever the primary classifier guessed (usually a nearby but wrong self-service/compound action) was left uncorrected. This is a real, customer-facing gap, not a security issue — no credential is ever misapplied to the wrong booking; the failure is "correct info, wrong destination."

**Fix**: extended `extractManageLinkCredentialsFromPrompt` in [`ai-manage-booking-with-token.util.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-manage-booking-with-token.util.ts) with a free-text fallback — `FREE_TEXT_BOOKING_ID_PATTERN` / `FREE_TEXT_MANAGE_TOKEN_PATTERN` — anchored to the real shapes these values actually have in this system (bookingId = UUID; manageToken = `generateBookingManageToken()`'s 48-char lowercase hex), so it can't false-positive on ordinary sentences that merely mention "booking id" or "token" without a real value attached. The existing URL-regex is tried first; the free-text pattern is only a fallback. No change was needed to `rescueManageBookingWithTokenIntent` itself — once credentials are detected, its existing cancel/reschedule/explain routing logic (already covered by e2e-bug.106/134/103's tests) just works.

**Verification**:
1. Live re-test after the fix, same fake credentials: all 3 previously-broken free-text phrasings now correctly reach `cancel_booking_with_token` / `reschedule_booking_with_token` / `explain_manage_booking_context`, with the identical `"Booking not found"` response the URL-paste path already gave — the two input styles are now symmetric.
2. Regression-checked the URL-paste path still works unchanged; checked case-insensitivity (upper-cased UUID/token in free text still extracts correctly); checked a genuinely credential-free prompt (`"What is my booking id?"`) does **not** get hijacked — confirms the anchored regex isn't over-broad.
3. New test suite in `ai-manage-booking-with-token.util.spec.ts` (`e2e-bug.102` describe block, 6 new tests): extraction from natural phrasing, labelled-field phrasing (`bookingId: X token: Y`), case-insensitivity, partial extraction (bookingId present without a token), the false-positive guard, and full `rescueManageBookingWithTokenIntent` routing for all 3 verbs using only free-text credentials.
4. Full `ai-manage-booking-with-token` test cluster: 31/31 pass. Ran the 4 other spec files that import this module (`ai-e2e103-package-visit-with-token`, `ai-e2e134-guest-manage-link`, `ai-e2e234-manage-token-page-context`, `public-booking-assistant-page-context.integration`) — 2 pre-existing failures found (both `reschedule`-with-manage-URL scenarios landing on `book_appointment`), confirmed via `git stash` to be identical with and without this fix, i.e. pre-existing and unrelated. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Not fixed here, out of scope: the classifier occasionally routing a *correctly-detected* prompt somewhere odd before the deterministic rescue overrides it is a separate, cosmetic non-issue (the rescue always wins); a genuinely un-anchored real bookingId/token pair typed with unusual formatting (e.g. split across multiple sentences) is not covered by this fix and would need a different approach (structured LLM param extraction rather than regex) if it turns out to matter in practice.

## web-booking-e2e-plan.1 — EXECUTION LOG

**Section A (page-by-page) — business landing page**: loaded cleanly, no console errors. Business header, "Best service" description card, "Any available specialist" quick-book card, and a live provider list with real-time slot grids (Gevorg Gasparyan, 3.5★/6 reviews, 18 real bookable time slots shown) all rendered correctly. "Booking assistant" FAB opens a chat panel with 2 page-specific suggested prompts ("What's the cheapest service?", "Who's free tomorrow?"), a mic button, and a text input. Confirmed clean so far.

**Section E/F — AI assistant widget, first live test — severe finding, e2e-bug.90 UI amplification**: sent `"what services do you offer?"` (the exact e2e-bug.90 trigger prompt) through the widget. Network tab confirms the identical backend `500` (`POST .../assistant` → 500, same `"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')"` payload as the curl reproduction). **The web UI has zero error-message sanitization on this path**: the raw JavaScript exception string is rendered **twice** — once as an inline chat bubble styled identically to a normal assistant reply (complete with a working "Listen" text-to-speech button that would read the raw exception aloud), and again in a separate bottom-of-screen toast reading `"Could not create. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')."` No console error was thrown (the fetch failure is caught somewhere), confirming this is a **display bug, not a crash** — the code path deliberately takes whatever error string it receives and shows it verbatim to the customer, in two different UI surfaces, with no generic fallback message ("Something went wrong, please try again") anywhere in between. A secondary, smaller defect: the toast's static prefix, `"Could not create."`, is wrong for this scenario — the failed action was a read/discovery query (`what services do you offer`), not a "create" operation, suggesting the toast copy is a generic catch-all mislabeled for creation-flow errors specifically. **This is a materially worse real-world manifestation of e2e-bug.90 than the raw-JSON API response already documented** — an API consumer seeing a JSON error is one thing; an end customer seeing a garbled JavaScript stack-trace fragment presented as the assistant's own words, with a "click to have it read aloud" affordance, is a much sharper UX failure. Not yet numbered — will fold into the closure pass with the rest of this plan's findings, likely as a direct amendment to e2e-bug.90 rather than a new number, since the root cause is identical.

**Working-prompt contrast confirmed**: `"tell me about your business"` rendered cleanly — correct `explain_salon_profile` content plus a "Continue booking" navigate button. Confirms the raw-error rendering above only occurs on the failure path; happy-path UI is otherwise well-built.

**Section E — booking_help / guide-flow rendering, and a major confirmation + expansion of e2e-bug.91**: sent `"how do I book with you?"` — rendered as a polished "Step 1 of 4: Select a Professional" guide card with step title/body and a "Next step" button, genuinely good UX. **Critically, the visible chat transcript does NOT show any of the internal debug fields** — confirming the widget's rendering code specifically extracts only `guide`/`summary`/`navigate` fields and doesn't dump the raw `sessionContext` object into the chat bubble. **However, pulling the raw network response for this exact request (`POST .../assistant` → 201) confirms e2e-bug.91's leak is still fully present at the network/API level**, fully exposed to anyone with browser dev tools open on this public page (a trivial bar for any customer). The full captured payload is significantly richer than the curl-based finding already on record:
- `_capabilityHints`: the **complete, verbatim raw LLM system prompt**, listing all ~220 native intent names plus the 14 delegated ones, plus the full internal architecture description ("Discovery/booking delegated to PublicBookingAssistantService...").
- `_entityMemoryBlock`: real per-business learned entity aliases — crucially including **a real customer's name**: `"mary" → customer=Mary`, alongside provider aliases (`"jujo" → provider=Jujo Karapetyan`, `"karo" → provider=Karo Mazmanyan`) and service aliases.
- **New sub-finding**: `_entityMemoryAliases` is leaked as the literal string `"[object Object]"` — a raw JS object was stringified with `String(obj)`/template interpolation instead of `JSON.stringify(obj)`, a small but concrete serialization bug on top of the exposure itself.
- **New, concerning sub-finding**: `_roleProfile: "owner"` is present on this request even though it's a fully anonymous, unauthenticated public call (`customerId: null`, `userEmail: null`). Not yet determined whether this reflects a real over-broad default-role resolution (a business-owner-level role profile being attached to anonymous public traffic) or just an internal default label with no functional effect — worth a source-level check in the fix pass, since "owner" attached to anonymous requests is a red flag regardless of functional impact.
- Also present: `_commandTraceId`, `_accessTier: "client"`, `_actorRole: "client"`, `_membershipRole: "client"`, `_planTierId: "business"`, `_scopedEmployeeId`, `_locationId`, `_branchHint`, `_confidenceHigh: "0.85"`, `_abVariantId`.

**Net effect for the closure pass**: e2e-bug.91 remains valid and serious — the leak is real and reproducible at the network layer regardless of the official web client's own (good) chat-rendering discipline — and now has a fuller field inventory plus 2 new sub-findings (`_entityMemoryAliases` serialization bug, anonymous-request `_roleProfile: "owner"`) worth folding into its write-up.

**Section A/L — guest manage-link page**: navigated directly to `manage?bookingId=<real>&token=<real>` (both fetched from the DB for the last remaining seeded booking) — the page correctly parsed both URL params and rendered a real, correct booking summary (facemassage, Gevorg Gasparyan, 19/07/2026 14:35–15:35) with "Reschedule"/"Cancel booking" buttons and a "Sign in with Google" prompt, all without any auth header. Confirmed clean for the base page render.

**New finding — the manage page's own AI widget suggested prompts don't correctly use page context**: this page's assistant shows 3 page-specific suggested prompts (`"Cancel this appointment"`, `"Reschedule to next week"`, `"Send manage link"`), implying the widget is meant to be context-aware of the specific booking already loaded on this page. Clicking `"Reschedule to next week"` — the page's own official, one-click suggestion — **did not trigger `reschedule_booking_with_token` at all**; it produced a generic `booking_help`/`guide_user_flow` response ("Here's how to book an appointment on this page: Pick a professional or choose Any available" / "Step 1 of 2"), completely ignoring that a specific existing booking (with a valid token) was already loaded on this exact page. This means even the manage page's own first-party, pre-written suggested action fails to resolve to the correct guest-token intent — a genuine, page-specific UI/classification bug distinct from anything found via curl this session (curl testing always had to explicitly engineer prompts to reach these intents; this is the *official, first-party, single-click path* on the real page failing on its own). Not yet root-caused (would need to inspect the actual request payload sent, not just the URL, to see whether `bookingId`/`manageToken` are threaded into the request at all) — worth flagging as a new, UI-specific finding for the closure pass, tentatively **e2e-bug.106** pending final numbering.

**e2e-bug.106 confirmed 2/2, not a one-off**: retried with a fully explicit, unambiguous free-typed prompt on the same manage page — `"reschedule this booking to tomorrow at 3pm"` — same result: generic `booking_help` guide, not `reschedule_booking_with_token`. Both requests returned `201 Created` (the backend classified and executed *something* successfully, just the wrong action) — ruling out a token-expiry/auth-rejection explanation. This strongly suggests the manage page's AI widget component simply never threads the already-loaded `bookingId`/`manageToken` into the AI request context at all, regardless of what the customer types — meaning **the entire guest-token reschedule/cancel flow is unreachable via this page's AI assistant, full stop**, independent of phrasing (customers can still use the plain "Reschedule"/"Cancel booking" buttons on this page directly, which don't go through the AI layer — this only affects the chat widget specifically). — **Fixed:** see Fix log entry under e2e-bug.107 / e2e-bug.106 FIXED summary.

### e2e-bug.106 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed across all 3 reproduced page types

Re-verified from scratch rather than trusting the inline "Fixed" note at face value. Confirmed the actual fix is in place by reading the current code, then re-ran live reproductions of all 3 originally-broadened instances (manage page, checkout page, and — via the shared code path — the multi-service availability page) against the real backend.

**Code confirmed still in place**: [`public-booking-assistant.tsx:190-195`](frontend/src/components/public-booking/public-booking-assistant.tsx#L190) builds `assistantPageContext` via `buildPublicAssistantPageContext(pathname, searchParams.toString())` on every submit and merges it into the request `context`.
