**e2e-bug.145 (severe) — an ordinary owner question crashes the endpoint with a raw, unhandled 500 that leaks a Postgres/TypeORM internal error message directly to the client.** — **Fixed:** `Customer.tags` is TypeORM `simple-array` (comma string), not a PG array — replace all `'waitlist' = ANY(c.tags)` with `simpleArrayTagMatchClause` / `andWhereSimpleArrayTag`; allow `waitlist` in `CUSTOMER_TAGS`; gateway `execute()` catch-all converts unexpected errors to `{success:false, action:'error'}` (HttpException still rethrows). Specs: `customer-tag-query.util.spec.ts`, `ai-waitlist-dashboard.logic.spec.ts`, `ai-gateway.service.spec.ts`. `"How many customers are on my waitlist?"` → HTTP 500, body: `{"statusCode":500,"message":"op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side","timestamp":"..."}` — no `success:false`/`action` envelope at all, a hard crash, not a graceful failure. This is a genuine, unremarkable question a real business owner would ask routinely, not an edge case. Root cause not fully traced to an exact line this pass, but the failure shape is clear: somewhere in whatever handler this classifies to (waitlist-domain, plausibly `coordinate_waitlist_offer` per [`ai-coordination.util.ts:28`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-coordination.util.ts:28) or a related waitlist-count query), a TypeORM query builder's `IN (:...ids)`/array-operator clause is being called with a non-array value (likely a single ID or `undefined` where an array was expected), which Postgres rejects at the SQL level with the literal `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side` error. Confirmed via source read that [`ai-command.controller.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-command.controller.ts) has **no try/catch at all** around its `return this.aiGateway.execute({...})` call (the same unguarded passthrough already documented for e2e-bug.135's pipeline-leak), so any unhandled exception anywhere in the entire AI pipeline propagates straight to NestJS's default exception filter and gets serialized verbatim into the HTTP response — meaning this specific crash is a symptom of a systemic gap (no error boundary around AI command execution at all), not an isolated one-off. Real-world impact: the dashboard AI assistant would show the user a raw backend crash message instead of any answer, for a completely ordinary question. Fix direction: (1) wrap the specific array/`IN`-clause query bug once located, and (2) more importantly, add a catch-all try/catch in `AiCommandController.execute()` (or the gateway) that converts any unhandled exception into a graceful `{success:false, action:'error', summary:'...'}` response instead of a raw 500 — this would have contained e2e-bug.145 as a "sorry, something went wrong" message instead of an internal-error leak, and would harden the endpoint against whatever the *next* undiscovered query bug turns out to be. **Reproduced a second time with different phrasing** — `"Show me the waitlist"` → the identical HTTP 500 / `"op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side"` — confirming this isn't a one-off fluke tied to specific wording but a deterministic crash for the entire waitlist-count/list domain on the dashboard surface.

**e2e-bug.145 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed, both original crash prompts and the systemic catch-all all hold.** Confirmed the gateway catch-all still exists ([ai-gateway.service.ts:186-205](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-gateway.service.ts:186)), tagged `e2e-bug.145` in a comment, still rethrowing genuine `HttpException`s while converting anything else to a graceful `{success:false, action:'error'}`. Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='customer-tag-query.util.spec|ai-waitlist-dashboard.logic.spec'` — **2 suites passed (2), 6 tests passed (6)** — and `npx jest --testPathPatterns='modules/ai/ai-gateway.service.spec'` — **1 suite passed (1), 28 tests passed (28)** (including the exact simulated `op ANY/ALL` scenario this bug originally reported, confirmed by the test's own logged error output matching the original crash message verbatim).

Live-reproduced both original repro prompts against the real running backend (owner JWT, `gevgas-operations-7c299253`), checking the raw HTTP status this time (not just the JSON body) since the original bug's defining symptom was the transport-level 500:
- `"How many customers are on my waitlist?"` → **HTTP 201** (not 500), `{"success":true,"action":"list_waitlist_entries","summary":"You have 4 customers on your waitlist: AI Cmd QA Customer, Mary Torgomyan, QA Web Single, and Test Customer.",...}`.
- `"Show me the waitlist"` → **HTTP 201**, `{"success":true,"action":"list_waitlist_entries",...}` — same 4 entries, same data.

Independently verified against the database (not just trusting the API response): `SELECT name, tags FROM customers WHERE business_id=... AND tags LIKE '%waitlist%'` → exactly 4 rows, matching the API's 4 names precisely. No raw Postgres/TypeORM error leaked anywhere; both queries return real, accurate data rather than merely failing gracefully. Purely read-only verification — no mutation, nothing to clean up. **Conclusion: e2e-bug.145 is genuinely fixed** — both the specific `simple-array`/`ANY()` query bug and the systemic missing-error-boundary gap it was originally used to justify are confirmed still resolved.

**e2e-bug.146 (distinct from e2e-bug.137) — a real, fully-built dashboard mutation action exists but the classifier never routes to it, sending the request to the tool-less react_agent instead, which then (at least honestly) declines.** — **Fixed:** added deterministic rescue for `create_location`/`update_location` (`rescueLocationsIntent` + classified/unknown wiring), `create_commission_rule`/`export_analytics_report` (retail-finance rescue + param parse), and fixed `configure_business_tax` rate parsing for `"8.5 percent"` (word form, not only `%`). `"Add a new business location called QA Test Branch at 123 Test St"` → `react_agent`: `"Adding a new business location is not supported by the current tools available."` — but this is false: `create_location` is a real, fully wired dashboard action (confirmed via `grep`: [`ai-locations-dispatch.build.ts:25`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-locations-dispatch.build.ts:25), [`ai-locations.logic.ts:53`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-locations.logic.ts:53), registered as a mutating intent in [`command-pipeline-mutating-actions.util.ts:112`](backend/src/modules/ai/command-pipeline-mutating-actions.util.ts:112) — built earlier this same session's coverage work). This is meaningfully different from e2e-bug.137's pattern (react_agent lacking tools for domains with *no* real dashboard action at all) — here the real action exists and is dispatch-wired, but the classifier failed to route to it and fell back to react_agent instead, which then correctly-but-misleadingly reports the *feature itself* as unsupported rather than a routing failure. A business owner reading this response would reasonably conclude the platform can't do multi-location management at all, when in fact it can — they just can't reach it through the assistant. Not root-caused to a specific classifier-confidence line this pass; flagged as a related-but-distinct investigation from e2e-bug.137, since fixing the tool-registry gap alone would not fix this (the real action already exists — the classifier itself needs to route to it).

**2nd confirmation, same session**: `"Update my main location's address to 456 New St"` → `react_agent`: `"I cannot update location addresses directly."` — `update_location` is equally real and dispatch-wired ([`ai-locations-dispatch.build.ts:28`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-locations-dispatch.build.ts:28)), confirming e2e-bug.146 affects the entire locations domain (both its mutations), not just `create_location` in isolation.

**e2e-bug.147 (a more dangerous variant — confident fabrication, not a denial) — when react_agent has no real tool for a question, it sometimes invents a generic, plausible-sounding answer dressed as business-specific data, rather than declining.** — **Fixed:** add `list_service_resource_requirements` read over `getServiceRequirements` (classifier + rescue + dispatch + react tool); extract serviceName from "what equipment does X require"; react_agent system prompt forbids inventing business-configured data from world knowledge. Specs/eval: `ai-schedule-resources.util.spec.ts`, `ai-schedule-resources.logic.spec.ts`, `ai-intent-rescue.service.spec.ts`, `ai-schedule-resources.integration.spec.ts`, `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E147_SERVICE_RESOURCE_REQUIREMENTS_CASES`. `"What equipment does the deep tissue massage service require?"` → `react_agent`: `"The deep tissue massage service typically requires a massage table, oils or lotions, towels, bolsters or cushions, and optionally hot stones or massage tools."` — confirmed via `grep` that `set_service_resource_requirements` ([`ai-schedule-resources-dispatch.build.ts:64`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-schedule-resources-dispatch.build.ts:64), built earlier this session) is **write-only** — no corresponding read/list action exists for querying a service's actual configured resource requirements. So the react_agent, with no data-access path at all (not even the react_agent's own tool list has a resource-requirements tool), fell back on the underlying LLM's generic training-data knowledge of what a massage "typically" needs, phrased indistinguishably from a real, business-specific answer (only the word "typically" hints this isn't grounded in this business's actual configuration). This is a materially worse failure mode than e2e-bug.137's flat refusals or even e2e-bug.139's mislabeled-real-data case: here there is no real underlying data at all, generic or otherwise — the entire answer is invented, and a business owner has no way to distinguish it from a real system lookup. Fix direction: (1) build a real read action for resource requirements (the write-only gap is itself a smaller finding), and (2) more broadly, the react_agent's system prompt should instruct it to explicitly decline rather than answer from general world knowledge whenever a question implies looking up business-specific configured data it has no tool for.

**e2e-bug.147 write-side follow-up (2026-07-30) — the flagged `set_service_resource_requirements` name-resolution gap is now fixed.** Root cause: `handleSetServiceResourceRequirementsLogic` ([`ai-schedule-resources.logic.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-schedule-resources.logic.ts)) already had working resource-name resolution for `params.resourceNames`, but it was unreachable whenever the classifier put a human-readable name straight into `params.resourceIds` instead — that branch trusted every `resourceIds` entry as a real UUID and passed it verbatim to the query layer, producing the raw `invalid input syntax for type uuid: "QA Massage Table"` leak. **Fixed** using this codebase's established `isUUID` idiom (same pattern as `uuid-param.util.ts`'s e2e-bug.117 fix): every `resourceIds` entry is now validated with `isUUID` from `class-validator`; non-UUID entries are treated as misclassified names, merged into `resourceNames`, and resolved case-insensitively (exact match first, then partial) against the business's real `scheduling_resources`, exactly like the existing `resourceNames` path. A genuine no-match now returns a clean `success:false` with `"None of the given resource names matched the catalog for \"<service>\"."` instead of a raw DB error.

Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='ai-schedule-resources.util.spec|ai-schedule-resources.logic.spec|ai-schedule-resources.integration.spec'` — **3 suites passed (3), 59 tests passed (59)** (56 previously + 3 new). `tsc --noEmit` clean for this change (confirmed no `ai-schedule-resources`/`isUUID`-related errors; the ~3200 unrelated pre-existing errors elsewhere in the repo were confirmed via `git stash` isolation to persist identically with this fix stashed out, so they're pre-existing baseline noise, not a regression from this change).

**3rd confirmation of e2e-bug.146** — `"Set commission rate for Gevorg Gasparyan to 20 percent"` → `react_agent`: `"I currently cannot set commission rates for employees."` — but `create_commission_rule` is a real, dispatch-wired dashboard action ([`ai-retail-finance-dispatch.build.ts:141`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-retail-finance-dispatch.build.ts:141), built earlier this session per the commission-rule-CRUD coverage work). **e2e-bug.148 — `create_product` fails to extract a plainly-stated price because its regex fallback only recognizes rigid `"price 5"`/`"retail 5"` number-adjacent forms, not natural phrasing like "priced at 5 dollars."** — **Fixed:** broaden `extractRetailPriceFromPrompt` ("priced at", "$N", "N dollars"); `enrichCreateProductParamsFromPrompt` sets both `price` + `retailPrice` + called-name; rescue enriches even when already `create_product`; validator accepts `retailPrice`. Specs/eval: `ai-retail-finance.util.spec.ts`, `ai-intent-rescue.service.spec.ts`, `ai-cmd-entity-completion.util.spec.ts`, `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E148_CREATE_PRODUCT_PRICE_CASES`. `"Add a retail product called QA Test Product priced at 5 dollars"` → `{"success":false,"action":"create_product","summary":"I need one more detail: Specify product price. Example: \"$18\"."}` — despite the price being unambiguously stated. Traced to [`ai-retail-finance.util.ts:325-330`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-retail-finance.util.ts:325) (`extractRetailPriceFromPrompt`): the only 2 supported patterns are `/\bretail\s+(\d+...)\b/i` (literal word "retail" immediately followed by a bare number) and `/\bprice\s+(\d+...)\b/i` (literal word "price" immediately followed by a bare number) — neither matches "priced at 5 dollars" (wrong word form "priced" vs "price", and the number is separated by "at" and followed by the word "dollars" rather than sitting bare). Note `handleCreateProductLogic` itself ([`ai-retail-finance.logic.ts:246`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-retail-finance.logic.ts:246)) actually defaults `retailPrice` to `0` rather than failing when unresolved, so the "specify product price" clarify response observed must originate from an earlier classifier-level required-field pre-check that also failed to extract a price from this phrasing — meaning the gap exists at 2 layers (LLM param extraction and the regex fallback) for the exact same natural phrasing style already shown to fail in e2e-bug.140/141 (expense category/description extraction) — this is the 4th session-documented instance of "plainly stated entity in natural phrasing fails to populate a handler param" this dashboard sweep alone. Fix direction: broaden the regex to accept `"priced at $X"` / `"for $X"` / `"X dollars"` forms, matching the flexibility already expected of `extractExpenseAmountFromPrompt` elsewhere in the same file. **Confirmed the trigger is specifically the spelled-out "dollars" form**: retrying with `"$5"` instead (`"Add a retail product called QA Test Product 2, price $5"`) succeeded immediately via the same `create_product` action.

**Clean pass — `mark_no_shows`** correctly used a two-step confirm-before-mutate pattern (`"Mark today's 9am booking as a no-show"` → `"You are about to mark today's 9am booking as a no-show. Please confirm to proceed."`) — not confirmed further since it would mutate a real, unrelated customer's booking status; noted as a positive example of a mutating dashboard action gating on explicit confirmation, unlike e2e-bug.136's `clear_schedule`.

Cleanup via `delete_inventory_product` reported success and was independently verified via a follow-up `list_products` call confirming the business's inventory is empty again — no lingering test data.

**e2e-bug.148 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — regex fix holds, but found and fixed a genuine, distinct regression in the deterministic rescue layer.** Confirmed the original regex broadening (`extractRetailPriceFromPrompt`, `enrichCreateProductParamsFromPrompt`) is unchanged and still correct — `ai-retail-finance.util.spec.ts` (17/17) and the targeted `ai-intent-rescue.service.spec.ts` create_product cases pass. However, running the **full** deterministic eval suite (`npx jest --testPathPatterns='ai-command-eval.spec'`, which exercises `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E148_CREATE_PRODUCT_PRICE_CASES` through the *real* `AiIntentRescueService.rescue()` starting from `action:'unknown'` — i.e. simulating total classifier failure, not just "classifier already got it right, only price extraction was tested") surfaced 2 genuine failures: `e2e148-priced-at-dollars` and `e2e148-price-dollar-sign` both resolved to `list_services`/`budget_list_services` instead of `create_product`.

**Root cause**: `rescueRetailFinanceIntent` already had a correct `isCreateProductPrompt` → `create_product` rescue path ([`ai-retail-finance.util.ts:885`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-retail-finance.util.ts:885)), but it is called (`this.tryRescueRetailFinance`, line 1611/2734) *after* the budget-service-discovery rescue (`this.tryRescueBudgetServiceDiscovery`, line 980/1783) in both the classified and unknown rescue phases of [`ai-intent-rescue.service.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-intent-rescue.service.ts). `rescueBudgetServiceDiscoveryIntent` treats any unclassified/misclassified prompt containing a bare price mention (e.g. "5 dollars") as a budget-filter signal and short-circuits to `list_services` before retail-finance's own already-correct rescue ever runs — the exact same "steal-before-rescue" ordering bug already documented this session for e2e-bug.137 (customer retention vs. `leave_visit_review`) and e2e-bug.146 (business tax vs. `leave_visit_review`), just against a different domain pair (create_product vs. budget-discovery).

**Fix** (mirrors the established e2e-bug.146/137 rescue-before-steal pattern, plus the existing `isCreatePromoCodePrompt` exclusion precedent already used inside `rescueBudgetServiceDiscoveryIntent` for the same reason): (1) added a new early-guard private method `tryRescueCreateProductEarly` in `ai-intent-rescue.service.ts`, called immediately before both `tryRescueBudgetServiceDiscovery` call sites (classified-phase and unknown-phase), that rescues straight to `create_product` (via `enrichCreateProductParamsFromPrompt`) whenever `isCreateProductPrompt` matches and the action isn't already `create_product`; (2) added `isCreateProductPrompt` to `rescueBudgetServiceDiscoveryIntent`'s own exclusion list in `ai-budget-service-discovery.util.ts`, alongside the existing `isCreatePromoCodePrompt` guard, as defense-in-depth for any other call path.

This regression fix required no new unit tests beyond what `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E148_CREATE_PRODUCT_PRICE_CASES` already covers, since that eval suite is precisely the "classifier completely fails" adversarial case that caught this. Ran `tsc --noEmit` — zero new errors in `ai-intent-rescue.service.ts` / `ai-budget-service-discovery.util.ts` (confirmed pre-existing, unrelated errors elsewhere via `git stash` isolation, byte-identical before/after). Ran the full deterministic eval suite before and after the fix and diffed the failing-case-ID lists: **the only difference is `e2e148-priced-at-dollars` and `e2e148-price-dollar-sign` disappearing — zero new regressions introduced** (2 pre-existing, unrelated compound-decomposition failures remain, confirmed unrelated to this domain).

Guru-QA edge-case sweep, all live: `"...price $12.50"` → `retailPrice:"12.50"` (decimal + $ sign); `"...priced at 3000 AMD"` → `retailPrice:"3000.00"` (non-USD currency phrasing, already supported); a genuine no-price prompt (`"Add a retail product called QA Test Product 148C"`) → clean `success:false` clarification ("Specify product price. Example: \"$18\"") rather than a crash or a budget-discovery misroute. Independently confirmed via `psql`: all 3 successfully-created rows present with exact expected `retail_price` values (`5.00`, `12.50`, `3000.00`).

Not traced to an exact file/line this pass (multiple modules reference `start_time`-shaped identifiers: `booking.service.ts`, `service-packages.service.ts`, `scheduling-resources.service.ts`, `multi-service-booking-group.entity.ts` — narrowing to the exact tour-query call site would need a stack trace, unavailable from the HTTP response alone). **This is the 2nd distinct raw-500 crash found this dashboard sweep** (after e2e-bug.145's waitlist crash), both on completely ordinary questions, both fully explained by the same missing-error-boundary root cause — strengthening the case that a catch-all try/catch around `AiCommandController.execute()` should be treated as a priority fix independent of hunting down each individual query bug, since it's very likely more undiscovered query bugs exist elsewhere in this large, mostly-untested action surface (only a small fraction of 252 registered intents have been exercised this session) and each one currently crashes with a raw internal-error leak rather than a graceful failure.

## e2e-bug.250 — `list_tour_calendar_week` misparses a trailing prompt fragment ("I have this week") as `serviceName` — **Fixed**

Found while re-verifying e2e-bug.149. `"What tour bookings do I have this week?"` (a plain, unscoped question with no tour/service name mentioned at all) → `list_tour_calendar_week` succeeds correctly (real empty-state data, no crash), but `sessionContext.serviceName` is populated with `"I have this week"` — a nonsense fragment of the prompt, not a real tour/service name.

**Root cause**: `parseListTourCalendarWeekFromPrompt` trusted `params.serviceName` from the classifier without a plausibility check, and `attachSessionToResult` / `buildSessionContext` preferred that enriched fragment over the handler's cleared `details.serviceName: null`.

**Fix (2026-07-31)**:
- `isPlausibleTourServiceNameFilter` rejects fragments (`I have this week`, stopword-only, trailing week clauses); wired into parse + `extractServiceFilter`
- `buildSessionContext` drops implausible `serviceName` for `list_tour_calendar_week`
- `attachSessionToResult` prefers explicit handler `details.serviceName` (including `null`) over classifier enrichedParams
- Also: do not strip trailing singular `tour` from captures (kept `City tour`); broaden week-list detection for voice / "tour calendar" phrasing
- Specs: `ai-e2e250-tour-calendar-service-name.*` + util regression; live `frontend/scripts/qa-e2e-bug-250.mjs`

**Residuals filed**: some near-synonym prompts still crash with `Invalid time value` after classifying to `list_tour_calendar_week` — **e2e-bug.270** (out of scope for the sessionContext fragment bug).

Milder than e2e-bug.147 (this is at least grounded in real data, just the wrong data for the question asked) but the same underlying shape: react_agent has a tool that returns *some* schedule-adjacent data and uses it even when it doesn't actually answer what was asked, rather than recognizing the mismatch. Not independently numbered — folded conceptually alongside e2e-bug.147 as the same "wrong-but-plausible react_agent answer" family; not pursued further given the volume of higher-severity findings already documented this sweep.

**e2e-bug.150 (severe, precisely root-caused) — 3 real orchestration-tier dashboard actions (`optimize_schedule`, `resolve_conflicts`, `reassign_cancelled`) return the raw user prompt text as their `action` field instead of the canonical action name, on every single outcome (success, failure, and rejection alike).** — **Fixed:** `runOrchestrationIntent` takes canonical `action` separate from free-text `intent`; `taskToResult` maps `AgentType` → dashboard action so approve/retry never echo the prompt. Specs: `command-orchestration.service.spec.ts`, `ai-dashboard-depth.integration.spec.ts`. `"Can you rebook the customers who cancelled recently?"` → `{"success":true,"action":"Can you rebook the customers who cancelled recently?","summary":"Currently, there are no available slots to rebook customers who have recently cancelled..."}` — the `action` field contains the verbatim prompt string, not `reassign_cancelled`. Confirmed via the response's own `pipelineTrace`, which shows the classifier pipeline correctly resolving to `reassign_cancelled` at every stage (`classify → reassign_cancelled`, ..., `resolve → reassign_cancelled`) — so classification itself is entirely correct; the corruption happens strictly in how the final result object is assembled. Root-caused precisely: [`ai-command.service.ts:2045-2055`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-command.service.ts:2045) (the `case 'reassign_cancelled':` branch) calls `this.orchestration.runOrchestrationIntent({..., intent: effectivePrompt, ...})`, passing the **raw prompt string** as `intent`. [`command-orchestration.service.ts:68`](backend/src/modules/ai/command-orchestration.service.ts:68) then calls `this.taskToResult(task, params.intent)` — forwarding that same raw prompt string into `taskToResult`'s `action: string` parameter. [`command-orchestration.service.ts:111-186`](backend/src/modules/ai/command-orchestration.service.ts:111) (`taskToResult`) uses this `action` parameter verbatim in **every branch** (`REJECTED`, `FAILED`, `COMPLETED`, and the default requires-approval branch) with no override to the real, statically-known action name — so this is not an edge case, it is the unconditional behavior for every response from these 3 actions. Confirmed via `grep` that all 3 orchestration-tier case blocks in `ai-command.service.ts` (`optimize_schedule` at line 2021, `resolve_conflicts` at line 2033, `reassign_cancelled` at line 2045) share the identical `intent: effectivePrompt` pattern, so all 3 are affected identically. Real-world impact: any downstream code that keys behavior off the `action` field — client-side icon/UI selection, analytics/logging aggregation by action name, mutating-action allowlist checks, compound/multi-step orchestration inspecting a prior step's resolved action — would silently fail to recognize these 3 actions, since `action` never equals any of their real names; it's always whatever arbitrary text the user happened to type. Fix direction: at each of the 3 call sites in `ai-command.service.ts`, pass the literal action name (already known from the `case` label) instead of `effectivePrompt` — e.g. `runOrchestrationIntent({..., intent: effectivePrompt, ...})` should separately track the action name and pass it through to `taskToResult`, or `runOrchestrationIntent`/`taskToResult` should accept an explicit `action` parameter distinct from the free-text `intent` used for LLM processing.

**Also confirmed clean**: `"Which of my customers are VIP?"` → `summarize_customers`, correct action name and accurate real data (Gevorg Gasparyan, Gvidon Papi — matches VIP segment data seen earlier in this sweep's `list_customers` results). No `guide_user_flow` internal-field leak (`_capabilityHints`/`_entityMemoryBlock`/etc., the e2e-bug.91 pattern) reproduced on the dashboard surface when `"Where are the biggest gaps in my schedule this week?"` fell through to `guide_user_flow` — checked specifically given e2e-bug.91's prior customer-surface findings; the dashboard instance of this fallback does not carry the same leak.

Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='command-orchestration.service.spec|ai-dashboard-depth.integration.spec'` — **2 suites passed (2), 9 tests passed (9)**.

**Went further — read `CommandOrchestrationService` itself, not just the 3 call sites, since the original write-up's fix direction only covered where the action name enters the system, not what happens to it downstream.** Found a second, independent layer of protection already in place: `resolveResultAction()` ([`command-orchestration.service.ts:123-133`](backend/src/modules/ai/command-orchestration.service.ts:123)) always prefers a static `ORCHESTRATION_AGENT_RESULT_ACTIONS[task.agentType]` mapping over whatever `actionHint` string it's handed, falling back to the hint only if `agentType` is unrecognized. This matters because `approveTask()`, `retryFailedStep()`, and `executePlan()` — the 3 other entry points into `taskToResult()` beyond the original 3 `case` blocks — still pass `task.intent`/`params.plan.intent` (the raw free-text prompt) as the hint, not a literal action name. Wrote a throwaway debug script calling `resolveResultAction()` directly to confirm this guard actually works as designed: with a recognized `agentType` (e.g. `CANCELLATION_RECOVERY`), a raw prompt string passed as the hint (`"Please rebook everyone who cancelled"`) is correctly overridden to the canonical `"reassign_cancelled"`; only with an *unrecognized* `agentType` does the raw hint pass through unchanged (expected — nothing to map it to). This means the approve/retry/plan-execution paths for these 3 actions were never actually vulnerable to this bug in practice, even though they superficially still "pass the raw prompt as `actionHint`" — the type-based resolution catches it before it reaches the client. Debug script deleted after use.

Live-reproduced all 3 of the original bug's repro prompts against the real running backend (owner JWT, `gevgas-operations-7c299253`): `"Please optimize the schedule for Gevorg this week to reduce gaps"` → `{"action":"optimize_schedule","success":true}`; `"Detect and resolve any double-booking conflicts today"` → `{"action":"resolve_conflicts","success":true}`; `"Can you rebook the customers who cancelled recently?"` → `{"action":"reassign_cancelled","success":true}` — all 3 now correctly return their canonical action name, not the verbatim user prompt. `tsc --noEmit` clean for both touched files (the only errors found were pre-existing, unrelated ones in `customer-ai-command.service.spec.ts`, matched only by a substring coincidence in the grep, not the actual `ai-command.service.ts`/`command-orchestration.service.ts` files). **Conclusion: e2e-bug.150 is genuinely fixed**, and more robustly than the original 3-call-site fix alone suggested — the `resolveResultAction()` type-based override provides a second, independent safety net covering every other code path that produces a result for these 3 orchestration actions.

**Found a new, distinct sibling bug while probing phrasing variants — logged separately as e2e-bug.251, not fixed here (out of scope for this ticket).** `"Add a new catalog category named QA Nails"` (a natural synonym — "catalog category" instead of "service category" — for the exact same intent this ticket already fixed) → misroutes to `import_services_from_menu` (`"I need one more detail: Menu text is required..."`), a completely unrelated bulk-menu-OCR-import action. Root cause: `isImportServicesFromMenuPrompt`'s regex ([`ai-operations.util.ts:141-155`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-operations.util.ts:141)) matches `/\b(import|add|create)\b.+\b(?:menu|catalog|photo|image|ocr)\b/i` — any "add"/"create" prompt containing the bare word "catalog" anywhere later in the string, with no category-phrasing exclusion analogous to the one `isCreatePromoCodePrompt` already has for this exact scenario. See e2e-bug.251 below for the full write-up.

## e2e-bug.251 — "Add a new catalog category named X" misroutes to `import_services_from_menu` instead of `create_service_category` — **Fixed**

Found while guru-QA re-verifying e2e-bug.151. That ticket fixed the exact same intent for "service category" phrasing (`isCreateServiceCategoryPrompt` / `isCreatePromoCodePrompt`'s exclusion), but never touched the sibling `isImportServicesFromMenuPrompt` check, which has no equivalent guard.

`"Add a new catalog category named QA Nails"` (live, `gevgas-operations-7c299253`) → `{"success":false,"action":"import_services_from_menu","summary":"I need one more detail: Menu text is required…"}` with `partialParams.categoryName: "QA Nails"` — entity extraction was fine; action classification was wrong.

**Root cause**: `isImportServicesFromMenuPrompt` matched `/\b(import|add|create)\b.+\b(?:menu|catalog|…)\b/i`, so bare "catalog" inside "catalog category" stole the intent. Operations rescue also runs *before* catalog rescue, so catalog could not steal back once import won. Separately, `isCreateServiceCategoryPrompt` only allowed optional `service` before `category`, not `catalog`.

**Fix (2026-07-31)**:
- `isImportServicesFromMenuPrompt` — exclude `(service|catalog) category` / bare `add|create … category` unless a real menu/OCR signal is present
- `isCreateServiceCategoryPrompt` + name extract — accept `catalog category` synonym (e2e-bug.151 sibling)
- Specs: `ai-e2e251-catalog-category-not-menu-import.*`, ops/catalog/rescue regressions; eval cases under e2e151/251; live `frontend/scripts/qa-e2e-bug-251.mjs` **11/11**

**Residuals filed**: voice "named X … please" can drop trailing tokens from `categoryName` — **e2e-bug.271**.

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 12

**e2e-bug.152 — the exact same prompt, verbatim, routes to a completely different action on repeated asks, flipping between a correct real-data answer and a flat denial.** — **Fixed:** `isListClinicTasksPrompt` no longer matches "pending AI agent tasks" (broad pending+tasks steal); agent-ops rescue runs before clinic-tasks rescue; correct `list_agent_tasks` classifications are not overwritten. Specs/eval: `ai-agent-ops.util.spec.ts`, `ai-provider-clinic-tasks-and-results.util.spec.ts`, `ai-intent-rescue.service.spec.ts`, `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E152_PENDING_AI_AGENT_TASKS_CASES`. `"Show me pending AI agent tasks"` — earlier this same sweep (round 2), this exact phrasing correctly resolved to `list_agent_tasks` and returned a real number ("You currently have 50 open support tickets" — see e2e-bug.139's writeup, same underlying `list_agent_tasks` call). Re-asked now, verbatim, 3 consecutive times: all 3 attempts resolved to `react_agent` instead, and all 3 denied having any access at all (`"I currently do not have access to any pending AI agent tasks or a task management system. My focus is on managing salon/spa bookings and schedules."`). Each of these is a stateless, independent HTTP request (fresh curl call, same JWT, no shared client-side session/conversation history), so this isn't explainable by conversational drift on the client side — the server-side classification step itself is non-deterministic for identical input, flipping between correctly dispatching to a real, registered action (`list_agent_tasks`) and falling through to the tool-less `react_agent` fallback. This is a materially different and arguably more concerning finding than anything else logged this sweep: every other misclassification/routing bug found so far has been *consistently* wrong for a given prompt (reproducible, deterministic, traceable to a specific rule or regex gap) — this is the first confirmed case of the *same* prompt non-deterministically landing on two entirely different, semantically opposed outcomes (one correct, one a denial) purely from re-asking. Most likely explanation: LLM sampling variance at the classification step combined with a confidence threshold that sits right at the boundary for this particular prompt shape, sometimes clearing the bar for `list_agent_tasks` and sometimes not, falling through to `react_agent` when it doesn't. Fix direction: lower the classifier's temperature (or increase determinism via other means) for action-classification specifically, and/or lower `list_agent_tasks`'s effective trigger threshold so it doesn't sit on a knife's edge for such a literal, unambiguous phrasing — a business owner should get the same answer every time they ask the identical question. **Control check**: re-ran `"List customers who have not visited in 60 days"` (an earlier confirmed-clean prompt) 3 times — all 3 landed on `list_customers` consistently, showing this non-determinism isn't universal across all prompts, just specific borderline-confidence ones like this one — which makes the finding more concerning, not less, since it means the instability is silent and prompt-specific rather than an obvious global flakiness a developer would catch in casual testing.

**e2e-bug.152 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed, including the specific non-determinism the original bug was about.** Confirmed `isListClinicTasksPrompt` still excludes `"pending AI agent tasks"`/`"agent tasks"`/`"task queue"` phrasing ([`ai-provider-clinic-tasks-and-results.util.ts:121-133`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-provider-clinic-tasks-and-results.util.ts:121)), tagged with the original e2e-bug.152 comment. Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='ai-agent-ops.util.spec|ai-provider-clinic-tasks-and-results.util.spec'` — **2 suites passed (2), 54 tests passed (54)**; the dedicated e2e152 cases in `ai-intent-rescue.service.spec.ts` also pass (8/8).

**Since this bug's entire premise was non-determinism across repeated identical requests, a single live call proves nothing — re-ran the exact original repro prompt 8 consecutive times** (fresh stateless HTTP requests, same JWT, no shared session, against the real running backend, `gevgas-operations-7c299253`): `"Show me pending AI agent tasks"` → all 8/8 attempts consistently resolved to `{"action":"list_agent_tasks","success":true}` — zero flips to `react_agent`, zero denials. Also re-ran a second phrasing from the fix's own exclusion list, `"What is in my AI agent task queue?"`, 3 consecutive times — all 3 consistently `list_agent_tasks`. Regression guard: `"What are my pending clinic tasks?"` still resolves to a real, distinct action (`explain_clinic_services`, a sensible vertical-mismatch decline for this non-clinic business) rather than being swallowed by the agent-tasks exclusion in the other direction. `tsc --noEmit` clean for both touched files.

**Conclusion: e2e-bug.152 is genuinely fixed** — the specific non-determinism this ticket reported (the same prompt flipping between a correct real-data answer and a flat denial) no longer reproduces across repeated live calls, and the underlying classification is now stable for this prompt shape. No test-data mutations this pass (all requests were reads).

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 18

**e2e-bug.153 (SEVERE — the most business-critical finding of this sweep) — asking "How many customers do I have?" in plain English correctly resolves to the real `summarize_customers` action, but returns a headline customer count that is wrong by more than 20×, stated with total confidence.** — **Fixed:** force unqualified roster totals (`isUnscopedCustomerCountPrompt`) → `customerMetric=overview` before trusting classifier `most_no_shows` params; rescue `unscoped_customer_count`; ranked summaries always state `totalCustomers` so row count ≠ roster total; skip LLM enrich for `summarize_customers`; classifier/phrasing/eval wired. Specs: `ai-customer-metrics.spec.ts`, `ai-structural-extractors.spec.ts`, `ai-provider-availability.integration.spec.ts`, `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E153_UNSCOPED_CUSTOMER_COUNT_CASES`. `"How many customers do I have?"` → `{"success":true,"action":"summarize_customers","summary":"You have one customer, Gvidon papi, who has 1 no-show out of 3 total appointments and is in the VIP segment."}`. This business has **at least 22 real customers** (directly enumerated with names/IDs earlier this same sweep via a working `list_customers` call in round 6 — Token Test, Cancel Race Test, Solo Test, Race Test 1/2/3, AI Cmd QA Customer, Gift Redeem Test, 2× Package UI Test, Repro Test Single, Concurrency Test User, Test Customer, Mary Torgomyan, Ghazap parpeci, casns naskc, Gevorg Gasparyan, Gev Gas, Makich, Karen Karapetyan, and more), yet this response confidently states the business has exactly **one**. Root-caused via source read of [`ai-booking-core.service.ts:1180-1258`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-booking-core.service.ts:1180) (the `summarize_customers` handler) and [`ai-metric-resolvers.util.ts:131-151`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-metric-resolvers.util.ts:131) (`resolveCustomerMetric`): the handler supports 9 distinct metrics, of which exactly one — `'overview'` — actually reports `summary.totalCustomers` (the real, correct total business owners would expect from "how many customers do I have"); every other metric (`most_no_shows`, `most_bookings`, `most_cancellations`, `at_risk`, `high_no_show`, `vip`, `top_spenders`, `new_customers`) returns a **ranked, filtered sub-list** for a specific narrow criterion, not a total count. The response's phrasing ("1 no-show out of 3 total appt(s)") matches exactly the per-row detail format used for the `most_no_shows`/default-overview-rows metric, not `overview`'s own summary line (`"${summary.totalCustomers} active customers"`) — meaning this request resolved to a *ranked* metric (most likely `most_no_shows`, given the exact phrasing match) rather than `'overview'`, and the query legitimately found only 1 customer with any recorded no-shows (consistent with the earlier round-6 `list_customers` dump, where every listed customer showed `noShowCount: 0`). The failure is therefore compound: (1) a generic, unqualified "how many customers" question should unambiguously resolve to `'overview'`, not a niche no-shows ranking, and (2) even granting that misrouting, the final natural-language summary-generation step then compounds it by treating "1 customer appeared in this narrow no-show ranking" as if it meant "you have exactly 1 customer in total" — a severe semantic conflation between a filtered list's row count and the business's actual total customer count. Real-world impact: this is about as core and foreseeable a business-owner question as exists on this entire platform, and the answer is not just imprecise but actively, confidently false in a way that could shape real business decisions (an owner reading "you have one customer" might reasonably panic about customer retention when the actual number is 20+×). Fix direction: (a) ensure generic/unqualified "how many customers" phrasing resolves to `'overview'` in `resolveCustomerMetricFromSemantic`, and (b) independently, the summary-generation layer should never state a ranked sub-list's row count as if it were a total customer count — these are two different, both-necessary fixes.

Cumulative dashboard sweep total across all 18 rounds: **23 new numbered bugs (e2e-bug.135–153)**.

Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='ai-customer-metrics.spec|ai-structural-extractors.spec|ai-provider-availability.integration.spec'` — **3 suites passed (3), 108 tests passed (108)**.

**Since the write-up itself documented this bug as intermittent/prompt-shape-specific (line 3155's "did not reproduce... this time" note), a single live call can't confirm the fix — re-ran the exact original repro prompt 5 consecutive times** against the real running backend (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`): `"How many customers do I have?"` → all 5/5 attempts consistently returned the real `overview` summary (`"Customer overview: • 74 active customers • 1 total no-shows... • 115 total cancellations..."`), never the old wrong "you have one customer" answer. Independently verified against the database: `SELECT count(*) FROM customers WHERE business_id=...` → **75 total rows**, of which **74 `isActive=true`** and 1 `isActive=false`** — confirming "74 active customers" is the *correct* number, not a new miscount (the 1-row gap from the raw table count is a legitimate active/inactive distinction, not a bug). Also re-ran the "in total" phrasing variant — same correct `overview` summary. `tsc --noEmit` clean for both touched files.

**Conclusion: e2e-bug.153 is genuinely fixed** — the unqualified "how many customers" question now consistently resolves to the real roster overview across repeated live calls, matching the database's actual active-customer count, with no recurrence of the old ranked-metric-row-count conflation. No test-data mutations this pass (all requests were reads).

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 19

**e2e-bug.154 (SEVERE — a second, structurally-distinct instance of e2e-bug.153's "unscoped total silently mishandled" theme) — asking for a booking count with no date qualifier returns 0, while the exact same question scoped to a specific window returns correct, large, real numbers.** — **Fixed:** rescue `"How many bookings do I have in total?"` → `summarize_bookings` with `bookingMetric=count` + `allTime` (never react_agent empty-day `list_appointments`); `resolveDateRange` treats booking "in total" as a wide all-time window; compose labels "all time"; react-agent `list_appointments` gains `allTime` + prompt guard; skip LLM rewrite for `summarize_bookings`. Specs/eval: `ai-dashboard-summarize-bookings.logic.spec.ts`, `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E154_UNSCOPED_BOOKING_COUNT_CASES`. Original: `"How many bookings do I have in total?"` → `react_agent`: `"You currently have a total of 0 bookings."` — flatly false; this business has dozens of real bookings (accumulated across this entire session's testing, plus pre-existing seed data). Immediately re-asked with explicit scope: `"How many bookings do I have this week?"` → `"This week, you have a total of 32 bookings."`; `"How many bookings do I have today?"` → `"You have a total of 6 bookings today, with 5 confirmed and 1 cancelled..."` (both plausible and consistent with earlier utilization data this sweep). Root-caused structurally via source: [`booking-tool-registry.service.ts:59-63`](backend/src/engine/langgraph/tools/booking-tool-registry.service.ts:59) — the react_agent's **only** booking-listing tool, `list_appointments`, has a `schema: dateRangeSchema.extend(...)` — meaning the tool has no "all bookings, ever" mode at all; every call is inherently bounded to some date range. When the user's question carries no explicit date ("in total"), the LLM must supply *some* range to satisfy the required schema, and it silently picks one narrow enough to return an empty result — then reports that empty, arbitrarily-scoped result as if it answered the unqualified "in total" question, with no caveat that only a specific window was actually checked. This is the same broad failure shape as e2e-bug.153 (a totality/aggregate question gets silently answered by a narrower, differently-scoped query without disclosure) but with a different, independently-confirmed root cause (a tool-schema structural limitation rather than a metric-selection/summary-generation bug) — strong enough overlap that this pattern ("what happens when a business owner asks for a plain, unqualified 'how many X do I have' with no scope given") deserves a dedicated audit across every summarize/count-style dashboard action, since 2 independent instances have now been found by accident in ordinary testing, both severe, both on core business metrics (customers, bookings). Fix direction: (a) give the react_agent tool registry a genuine all-time/unscoped query option (or clearly document that `list_appointments` always requires an explicit or defaulted range), and (b) the react_agent's system prompt should instruct it to ask for clarification (or explicitly state the date range it assumed) rather than silently substituting a scope the user never specified — the same fix direction already noted for e2e-bug.147's fabrication problem generalizes here too.

Did not fully trace the exact query to a precise reconciliation — this is a much lower-severity, different question from e2e-bug.154's actual reported symptom (a false, confidently-wrong **zero**), and the numbers here are plausible and non-zero, so not treated as a bug pending a clearer repro of an actually-wrong count.

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 20

**e2e-bug.155 (SEVERE — a 3rd instance of the "unqualified total silently wrong" theme, this time with an exceptionally clean, single-line root cause) — `summarize_customers` confidently reports "no cancellations" for a business with dozens of real cancellations, because the underlying summary object never computes a cancellation total at all, despite a full cancellation-ranking metric existing right next to it in the same function.** — **Fixed:** `getCustomerInsights` summary now includes `totalCancellations` (same reduce as `totalNoShows` over `byStatus[CANCELLED]`); overview / most_cancellations AI summaries surface it; total-cancellation prompts force `customerMetric=overview`; `CommandReasoningService` skips LLM rewrite for `summarize_customers` so it cannot invent "no cancellations". Specs: `customer-insights-cancellations.spec.ts`, `ai-customer-metrics.spec.ts`, `ai-structural-extractors.spec.ts`, `ai-provider-availability.integration.spec.ts` (e2e-bug.155). Original: `"How many cancellations have I had in total?"` → `summarize_customers`: `"You have had a total of 1 no-show across all customers. There are currently no cancellations reported."` — false; this business has had dozens of cancellations this session alone (round 5: "24 cancellations this week"; round 8: "37 cancellations this week"). Root-caused precisely via source: [`customer.service.ts:772-779`](backend/src/modules/customer/customer.service.ts:772) (`getCustomerInsights`'s `summary` object) computes exactly 5 fields — `totalCustomers`, `totalNoShows`, `atRiskCount`, `highNoShowCount`, `vipCount` — **no `totalCancellations` field exists at all**, even though the very next block, [`customer.service.ts:795-802`](backend/src/modules/customer/customer.service.ts:795) (the `most_cancellations` metric branch), proves cancellation data is fully available and correctly computable per-customer (`r.stats.byStatus[BookingStatus.CANCELLED]`) — it's simply never aggregated into the summary. So any unqualified "how many cancellations" question that resolves to the `overview`-style summary path has no real number to draw from, and the response generation confidently states "no cancellations reported" instead of either surfacing the real aggregate (trivial to add — same reduce pattern already used for `totalNoShows` one line above) or routing to the `most_cancellations` metric, which does have the data. This is the cleanest root cause of the 3 "unqualified total" bugs found this sweep (e2e-bug.153, e2e-bug.154, this one) — a single missing field in a single object literal — and further strengthens the case for the dedicated audit already recommended in e2e-bug.154's writeup: **3 independent "how many X in total" business questions, 3 confidently wrong answers, found without deliberately hunting for this pattern.** Fix direction: add `totalCancellations: enriched.reduce((n, r) => n + (r.stats.byStatus[BookingStatus.CANCELLED] ?? 0), 0)` alongside `totalNoShows` in the summary object, and surface it in `overview`'s summary lines in [`ai-booking-core.service.ts:1211-1216`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-booking-core.service.ts:1211).

**e2e-bug.155 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed, and this pass fully reconciled the exact reported number for the first time in this "unqualified total" bug family.** Confirmed `totalCancellations` is still computed in `customer.service.ts:125/803` and surfaced in `ai-booking-core.service.ts:1224/1250`, tagged with the original e2e-bug.155 comment. Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='customer-insights-cancellations.spec|ai-customer-metrics.spec|ai-structural-extractors.spec|ai-provider-availability.integration.spec'` — **4 suites passed (4), 113 tests passed (113)**.

**Re-ran the exact original repro prompt 5 consecutive times** against the real running backend (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`): `"How many cancellations have I had in total?"` → all 5/5 attempts consistently returned `"Customer overview: ... • 115 total cancellations across all customers ..."` — never the old false "There are currently no cancellations reported" answer. Independently confirmed against the database: raw `SELECT count(*) FROM bookings WHERE status='cancelled'` → **122**, not 115 — but unlike e2e-bug.154's partially-reconciled gap, this one traced to an exact, fully-confirmed explanation: **7 of those 122 cancelled bookings have `customer_id IS NULL`** (guest/anonymous bookings never linked to a customer record) — `122 - 7 = 115`, an exact match. Since `getCustomerInsights` is structurally a per-customer aggregation (it iterates customers and sums each one's booking stats), a cancelled booking with no linked customer is invisible to it by design, not a bug — this is a legitimate scope boundary of "cancellations across all *customers*," not a miscount. `tsc --noEmit` clean for both touched files.

**Conclusion: e2e-bug.155 is genuinely fixed**, and this pass additionally confirms the reported number is exactly correct once the customer-scoped nature of the metric is accounted for — no test-data mutations this pass (all requests were reads).

**Partial correction to e2e-bug.153's severity read**: a differently-worded customer-count question this round (`"Which customers have the most cancellations"`) correctly reported `"There are 22 active customers..."` — the real, correct total. This confirms e2e-bug.153's wrong "1 customer" answer was specifically tied to that prompt's particular metric-routing outcome (most likely `most_no_shows`), not a universal failure of `summarize_customers`'s customer-count reporting — the `overview` path, when actually reached, does correctly report 22. The bug's core finding (that *some* natural phrasings of "how many customers" route to a narrow ranked metric and misreport its row count as a total) stands unchanged; this just narrows which phrasings trigger it.

**Also clean pass** — `summarize_reviews` (`"How many reviews do I have in total?"` → "6 reviews, average rating 3.5 out of 5" — no independent verification performed, but no evidence of the unqualified-total pattern here; reviews aggregation appears to be a genuinely unscoped, non-date-bound query by nature, consistent with it not sharing the same structural gap as bookings/cancellations).

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 21: closing out the "unqualified total" theme

**Not miscounted, correctly declined** — `"How much revenue have I made in total?"` and `"How many gift cards have I sold in total?"` both → `react_agent`, flat honest refusals (already-known e2e-bug.137 domains: revenue, gift-card sales), not confidently-wrong numbers. Good to confirm the "unqualified total silently wrong" failure mode (e2e-bug.153/154/155) doesn't universally apply — these 2 domains fail safely (admit no access) rather than fabricating a zero or small number.

**Minor, safe-failure structural gap** — `"How many active customer subscriptions do I have in total?"` → `list_customer_subscriptions`, correctly asked to clarify (`"Specify which customer (e.g. \"List Anna's subscriptions\")."`) rather than answering wrong. Confirms `list_customer_subscriptions` is structurally a per-customer lookup tool with no business-wide aggregate mode — the same general shape as e2e-bug.154's date-range-required `list_appointments` tool, but this one fails safely by asking for the missing required parameter instead of silently substituting an empty/narrow scope and reporting it as the total. Not numbered as a bug, since asking for clarification is the correct behavior when a genuinely required scope is missing — flagged only as a minor feature gap (no business-wide subscription count exists) alongside the closely-related, already-numbered e2e-bug.146/154 findings.

This closes out the deliberate stress-test of the "unqualified total" pattern first surfaced in e2e-bug.153. Summary of that sub-investigation: 5 domains tested with unqualified "in total" phrasing — **3 failed severely (confidently wrong numbers: customers, bookings, cancellations)**, **2 failed safely (revenue, gift cards: honest refusal)**, **1 failed safely with a clarifying question (subscriptions)**. The 3 severe failures share a common shape (silently substituting a narrow/empty scope for an unqualified aggregate request) but 2 independently-confirmed root causes (a missing summary field for cancellations; a schema requiring a date range for bookings; a metric-routing miss for customers) — meaning this is a systemic *pattern*, not one shared bug, and the dedicated audit recommended in e2e-bug.154 remains the right next step for whoever picks up the fix backlog.

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 23

**e2e-bug.156 — a mutation *confirmation prompt* (the text a business owner reads right before approving a real batch write) contains a fabricated detail: a non-existent employee name attached to an operation that has nothing to do with employees.** — **Fixed:** action-scoped `sanitizeParamsForPreview(params, action)` allowlists drop fabricated `customerName` / `templateName` / `employeeName` on catalog mutates (`update_service_prices`, `create_services`, etc.); confirmation summary is built only from sanitized preview params (LLM reasoning kept in `details` only). Specs: `ai-execution-confirm.util.spec.ts` (e2e-bug.156). Original: `"Create 3 new QA test services: QA Manicure at 20 dollars, QA Pedicure at 25 dollars, and QA Waxing at 15 dollars"` → `create_services`: `"You are about to create three new QA test services: QA Manicure at $20, QA Pedicure at $25, and QA Waxing at $15 **for Test User using the Standard Mon-Fri template**."` — "Test User" is not a real employee; this business's actual roster (confirmed via `list_employees` moments later) is Gevorg Gasparyan, Jujo Karapetyan, Mariam Ohanyan, and Karo Mazmanyan — no "Test User" exists anywhere. Nothing in the prompt named an employee or a schedule template, and plain service creation doesn't inherently involve either (employee-service linking is a separate action, `assign_employee_services`, tested successfully earlier this sweep). A near-identical retry with different service names (`QA Manicure2`/etc., to avoid a name collision) → the same `create_services` action, but this time the confirmation text correctly said nothing about any employee or template at all (`"You are about to create three new QA test services: ... Please confirm to execute this action."`) — a direct, same-action, near-identical-input reproduction showing the fabricated detail is not consistently present, the same non-deterministic-generation shape already documented in e2e-bug.152, but manifesting here as invented content in mutation-approval UI text rather than a routing flip. This is more concerning than a misrouted read, specifically because it's confirmation-prompt text: a real business owner deciding whether to approve a real write is being shown a plausible-sounding but entirely fictitious detail about who/what the operation affects, which could either cause needless confusion (an unrecognized name) or, worse, false confidence that the system correctly understood and scoped the operation to something specific when it did not. Neither test call was confirmed/executed (both left as pending `requiresExecutionConfirmation` previews), so no real services were created and no cleanup is owed. Fix direction: confirmation-prompt text generation for mutating batch actions should be built deterministically from the actual resolved parameters (which plainly don't include any employee/template for a bare `create_services` call), not generated freely by the LLM in a way that can inject unrelated, invented details.

**Round 33 update — the exact same "Test User" fabrication reproduced twice more, and this time proven to exist at the *structured parameter* level, not just in generated prose.** `"Increase the price of the QA Confirm Test service by 5 dollars"` (a real, single-service price update, created via `create_service` specifically for this test) → `update_service_prices`: confirmation text again said `"...for Test User"`, and critically, the raw `details.previewParams` object itself contained `{"serviceName": "QA Confirm Test", "customerName": "Test User", "templateName": "Standard Mon-Fri", "allProviders": false}` — a fabricated `customerName` field sitting in the actual structured data the confirmation is built from, not merely an artifact of free-text generation layered on top of clean params. Confirmed via `grep` that `"Test User"` does not appear anywhere in this codebase's classifier fixtures or defaults — it is not a hardcoded placeholder being echoed back; the model is inventing this value outright. Retried once more (same prompt, same service): reproduced again, `customerName: "Test User"` present a 2nd time (a 3rd attempt returned no `previewParams` at all, suggesting some non-deterministic branching in whether this field gets populated at all — consistent with e2e-bug.152's established non-determinism theme, but here affecting parameter population rather than action routing). This upgrades the finding's severity: since the fabricated value lives in `previewParams` — the structured object a client-side confirmation UI and, presumably, the eventual execution call would read from — this is not just cosmetic prose noise; it's a hallucinated field in the actual data contract between classification and execution for a mutating action, for a service-price-update request that has no legitimate concept of a "customer" at all. **Test-data note**: the `QA Confirm Test` service (created via `create_service` for this reproduction) was cleaned up via `deactivate_service` and independently verified via a direct `GET /businesses/:id/services` call confirming it no longer appears in the active catalog; the price-update confirmation itself was never approved/executed, so no price change ever took effect.

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 31

**Minor, honest partial-answer** — `"How many packages have been purchased this month?"` → `summarize_revenue_kpis`: gave real revenue/booking totals but explicitly admitted `"No packages have been specifically mentioned in the summary"` rather than fabricating a package-purchase count. Doesn't actually answer the question, but doesn't confidently invent a wrong number either — a safer failure mode than e2e-bug.153–155's pattern. Not numbered.

**4th confirmation of e2e-bug.138, and a new, more concerning variant — this time the customer-surface leak doesn't fail with "sign in," it silently succeeds and returns the wrong person's personal data.** `"List all my gift card bundles"` (a business-wide dashboard request) → `my_gift_cards`: `"You currently have gift cards available in your account."` Confirmed via `grep` that `my_gift_cards` is a customer-self-service action ([`ai-customer-crm-dispatch.build.ts:210`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-customer-crm-dispatch.build.ts:210), [`ai-customer-crm.logic.ts:826-834`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-customer-crm.logic.ts:826) — its own failure path literally says `"Sign in to view your gift cards."`, confirming it expects a customer session). Unlike the 3 prior e2e-bug.138 instances (which all failed closed with a "sign in" message), this one **succeeded** — because the test business owner (Gevorg Gasparyan) also exists as a real customer record in this same business's data (same name, same email, confirmed via the round-6 `list_customers` dump), so the system resolved a customer identity from the owner's own dual owner/customer account and returned *that person's own personal gift-card wallet* as if it answered "list all my [business's] gift card bundles." This is a materially different and arguably more concerning failure mode than the other e2e-bug.138 instances: instead of a confusing-but-harmless "sign in" dead-end, the dashboard silently returned real, but completely irrelevant, personal customer data in response to a business-management question, with no error or hint that the wrong data source was used. In a business where the owner does *not* happen to also be a customer, this exact path would presumably fail closed like the others — meaning this variant is data-dependent, but it demonstrates the underlying surface-boundary gap can silently produce wrong-but-plausible-looking answers, not just clean failures, depending on incidental overlap between owner and customer identities. Fix direction unchanged from e2e-bug.138 (constrain candidate actions to the current surface), but this instance strengthens the urgency, since "fails closed" was previously assumed to be the worst case for this bug family.

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 32: e2e-bug.156 strengthened to structured-parameter level, then an incident

**e2e-bug.156 update (see full entry above, round 30)** — **Fixed** (see e2e-bug.156). Test service (`QA Confirm Test`) created and cleaned up with independent verification; the price-update confirmation was never approved, so no real price change occurred from that test.

**e2e-bug.158 (SEVERE — process incident, unintended real mutation to pre-existing data)** — **Fixed:** `update_service_duration_buffer` is in `DASHBOARD_EXECUTION_CONFIRM_ACTIONS` (same gate as `update_service_prices`); confirmation preview includes `durationMinutes` / `bufferMinutes` / `serviceName`. Specs: `ai-execution-confirm.util.spec.ts` (e2e-bug.158). Original: while checking whether the confirmation-gating pattern generalized to a sibling action, `"Update the duration of the facemassage service to 45 minutes"` executed **immediately**, with no confirmation step at all, changing the real, pre-existing "facemassage" service (id `cd586065-cd4b-4416-8a0c-8e9985c3070c` — a genuine seeded catalog service, not a `QA Test...` row created for this session) to a 45-minute duration. This is a real bug in its own right — `update_service_prices` (tested moments earlier, same session, same catalog domain) correctly requires explicit confirmation before executing (`requiresExecutionConfirmation: true`, a `previewParams` object, "Please confirm to execute"), while `update_service_duration_buffer` — the same class of bulk/single catalog-mutating action — executes instantly on a single, unhedged natural-language request with no approval gate whatsoever. This inconsistency in which mutating dashboard actions require confirmation and which don't is itself a real product/safety finding, independent of the incident it caused here.

**Incident disclosure**: this was an unintended, real mutation to pre-existing business data, caused by testing this action without anticipating it would execute immediately (based on the sibling action's confirmation-gated behavior moments earlier). **The original duration of the "facemassage" service before this test is not recorded anywhere in this session's transcript** — no prior round captured its duration value — so it cannot be reverted with confidence, and no attempt was made to guess a value and "fix" it further, per the standing principle of stopping and disclosing rather than compounding an uncertain-state mutation. **The user was notified directly and immediately** when this was discovered, before any further mutation testing continued. Action needed from the business owner: check `facemassage`'s current duration (45 minutes) via the dashboard and restore it to its correct original value if 45 minutes is not correct. Fix direction for the underlying bug: `update_service_duration_buffer` should require the same explicit-confirmation gate that `update_service_prices` and other bulk catalog mutations already correctly implement, particularly since — per e2e-bug.156 — even the confirmation step itself cannot yet be fully trusted to contain accurate parameters, making a "no confirmation at all" path for this specific action doubly risky.

**e2e-bug.159 — asking to set up a personal, ongoing owner alert gets reinterpreted as a one-off customer-facing notification proposal, misunderstanding both who should be notified and about what.** — **Fixed:** rescue `"Notify me whenever a customer cancels…"` → `toggle_business_email_on_customer_change` with `enabled: true` (existing `notifyBusinessOnCustomerBookingChange` preference), not react_agent/`propose_notify_customers`. Detector + toggle extraction treat owner "notify/alert/email me whenever…" as enable; customer-outbound "notify the customer…" is excluded. Classifier NOT rules + react-agent guard. Specs/fixtures: `ai-e2e159-owner-cancel-alert.fixtures.ts`, `ai-push-notifications.util.spec.ts`, `ai-push-notifications.logic.spec.ts`, eval `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E159_OWNER_CANCEL_ALERT_CASES`. `"Notify me whenever a customer cancels a booking today"` (an owner asking to be alerted about *future* cancellation events — a subscription/preference-style request) → `react_agent`: `"A notification for the customer regarding their cancelled booking today has been proposed and is pending your approval."` — the system instead proposed sending a notification *to a customer* about *their own* already-cancelled booking, a completely different action addressing a different recipient about a different, already-past event, rather than any kind of recurring alert-for-the-owner concept (which may not exist as a real feature on this platform at all — an "ongoing alert subscription" is a different kind of feature than a one-off notification, and no evidence surfaced this sweep that the former exists). Confirmed via source read that the response carries `requiresApproval: true` and a real `taskId` — this was left as a pending, unapproved proposal, **not confirmed or executed**, so no actual customer notification was sent. Real-world impact if a real owner tried this: confusion at best (a notification about an unspecified, already-cancelled booking, addressed to an unspecified customer, requiring approval for something the owner didn't actually ask for) — and if approved without close reading, a real, unwanted message could go to a real customer for the wrong reason. Not root-caused to a specific line this pass; flagged for the fix backlog as a distinct misunderstanding-of-intent shape (recipient + tense/scope both wrong) rather than a simple misclassification.

Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='ai-push-notifications.util.spec|ai-push-notifications.logic.spec'` — **2 suites passed (2), 172 tests passed (172)**.

**Live-tested on the real running backend per this ticket's explicit ask** (owner JWT, `gevgas-operations-7c299253`): the exact original repro, `"Notify me whenever a customer cancels a booking today"` → `{"success":true,"action":"toggle_business_email_on_customer_change","summary":"Business email alerts are now enabled, and you will receive notifications when a customer cancels or reschedules their booking today.","details":{"notifyBusinessOnCustomerBookingChange":true}}` — correctly resolves to the owner-preference toggle, real setting flipped on, no customer-facing proposal, no `requiresApproval`/`taskId`. Root cause: `customerChangeCue`'s regex has a dedicated `a\s+customer\s+cancels?\b` alternative that explicitly handles the third-person-singular "-s" verb form for "cancel," but has no equivalent `a\s+customer\s+reschedules?\b` alternative for "reschedule" — so the exact same grammatically natural phrasing works for cancellations but not reschedules. See e2e-bug.252 below for the full write-up.

**Test-data cleanup**: this live pass toggled the real `notifyBusinessOnCustomerBookingChange` setting on and off several times while isolating the e2e-bug.252 regex gap (each toggle call is itself a real, persisted mutation, not a preview). ## e2e-bug.252 — owner alert toggle ("alert me whenever a customer reschedules") fails on the "-s" verb form that works for "cancels" — **Fixed**

Found while live-QA-verifying e2e-bug.159 with paraphrase edge cases. `customerChangeCue` had `a\s+customer\s+cancels?\b` but no `reschedules?` sibling, so `"Alert me whenever a customer reschedules"` fell through while `"… customers reschedule …"` worked.

- `customerChangeCue` — uniform `cancels?|reschedules?` for `a customer` / `customers?` / `when customers?`

- Specs: `ai-e2e252-owner-reschedule-alert.*`; live `frontend/scripts/qa-e2e-bug-252.mjs` **13/13** (setting restored to `notifyBusinessOnCustomerBookingChange=false`)

## AUDIT: confirmation-gating across all 202 dashboard-mutating actions (e2e-bug.161)

Commissioned directly in response to the 2 unintended real-data incidents this sweep (e2e-bug.158, e2e-bug.160). A dedicated research pass read `DASHBOARD_PIPELINE_MUTATING_ACTIONS` (202 entries, [`command-pipeline-mutating-actions.util.ts:15-218`](backend/src/modules/ai/command-pipeline-mutating-actions.util.ts:15)) and cross-referenced every entry against the codebase's actual confirmation-gating implementation.

**e2e-bug.161 (CRITICAL) — only 26 of 202 mutating dashboard actions (~13%) require explicit confirmation before executing; the remaining ~176 (~87%) execute immediately on a single natural-language request, and this is not a deliberate, reviewed policy — it's an inconsistent, seemingly incidental split.** — **Fixed:** replaced the inline `bulkConfirmActions` set with a registry-driven policy in `DASHBOARD_EXECUTION_CONFIRM_ACTIONS` / `requiresDashboardExecutionConfirmation()` (`ai-execution-confirm.util.ts`), wired through `AiCommandService` and `PRODUCT_GUIDE_BULK_MUTATE_ACTIONS`. Immediately gated `admin_delete_customer_data` (irreversible PII erase) to match `delete_customer_data` / `privacy_delete`, plus destructive/deactivate/delete, financial-config, credential/integration, compliance/HIPAA/breach, and the incident actions `update_service_duration_buffer` / `configure_cash_payments`. Specs: `ai-execution-confirm.util.spec.ts` (e2e-bug.161).

**Mechanism found**: exactly one general-purpose gate exists — the `bulkConfirmActions` `Set<string>` inline in [`ai-command.service.ts:1514-1537`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-command.service.ts:1514), which intercepts 22 named actions before dispatch and returns `requiresExecutionConfirmation: true`/`confirmationPrompt`/`previewParams` via [`ai-execution-confirm.util.ts:32-64`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-execution-confirm.util.ts:32). A further 4 actions build their own ad-hoc confirmation result inline in their own handler (`migrate_dashboard_date_display`, `notify_patient_result_ready`, `set_service_tax_rate`, `bulk_strip_disabled_locale_translations`). That's the complete list — **26 total**. Every other mutating action calls its underlying repository/service mutation directly and returns a plain `success(...)` with no gate at all. A separate, narrower gate (`isGuideHandoffMutatingAction`) blocks mutating actions only on the "product guide → do this for me" handoff path — irrelevant to the normal single-prompt dispatch path this entire QA sweep has used.

**Most severe individual finding — `admin_delete_customer_data` has zero confirmation gate.** This action anonymizes/erases real customer PII ([`ai-business-compliance.logic.ts:493-548`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-business-compliance.logic.ts:493)) and is **irreversible** — yet its own sibling actions, `delete_customer_data` and `privacy_delete`, ARE correctly gated. A single dashboard-owner prompt naming a customer could permanently erase their data with no confirmation step whatsoever, in stark contrast to the deliberately-gated version of essentially the same operation sitting right next to it in the registry.

**Other high-stakes ungated actions identified**: `configure_business_currency`, `configure_business_tax`, `configure_stacked_tax_rules` (silent changes to core financial configuration); `report_data_breach`, `send_breach_notification` (compliance-critical communications with no review step); `enable_hipaa_mode`, `configure_hipaa_session_timeout` (regulatory-mode toggles); `rotate_api_key`, `revoke_api_key`, `configure_stripe_connect` (credential/payment-integration changes — a misfired API key rotation or Stripe reconfiguration could break real payment processing instantly); `deactivate_service`/`deactivate_package`/`deactivate_subscription_plan` (confirmed directly reproducible this sweep — `update_service_duration_buffer` and `configure_cash_payments`, the 2 actions that actually caused this sweep's incidents, are both in this ungated majority); `unassign_employee_services`/`transfer_employee_services`; `delete_schedule_templates`; `toggle_annual_billing`.

**Domain-level pattern**: gating is concentrated almost entirely in **bulk booking/schedule operations** (`cancel_bookings`, `bulk_smart_cancel`, `clear_schedule`, `hide_appointments_from_calendar`, etc. — 11 of the 22 general-list entries) and **bulk catalog operations** (`create_services`, `update_service_prices`, `bulk_create_catalog`, etc.). Entire domains have **zero** gated actions at all: integrations/API keys, marketing/billing, gift cards, and (with the sole exception of the customer-privacy-delete pair) most of customer/CRM. This strongly suggests gating was added ad hoc, action-by-action or feature-by-feature, as specific bulk/high-volume operations were built — not as a deliberate security/safety policy applied consistently across the mutating-action surface.

**Fix direction**: (1) immediately gate `admin_delete_customer_data` to match its sibling actions — this is the single highest-priority item, given it's irreversible PII erasure; (2) establish a deliberate policy for which categories of action require confirmation (destructive, irreversible, financial-configuration, and credential/integration changes are the clear candidates) and apply it as a registry-driven check rather than continuing to add gates ad hoc per action; (3) audit the ~176 ungated actions against that policy rather than assuming today's 26-action list reflects considered risk assessment, since the evidence (2 real incidents in this sweep alone, from 2 of the ~176) suggests it does not.

**Session note**: given this audit confirms confirmation-gating is the exception rather than the rule across this action surface, further exploratory mutation testing against this dashboard should treat every untested mutating action as "executes immediately with no safety net" by default, not as "probably gated like the ones tested so far."
